events_in_windows.name: events_in_windows
events_in_windows.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, "_" , CAST(event_timestamp AS STRING)) AS event_id,
  event_timestamp,
  user_pseudo_id AS pseudo_user,
  -- engagement_time: try to extract from event_params where key='engagement_time' as int (seconds)
  (SELECT
     COALESCE(
       CAST(ep.value.int_value AS INT64),
       SAFE_CAST(ep.value.string_value AS INT64)
     )
   FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS ep
   WHERE ep.key = 'engagement_time'
   LIMIT 1) AS engagement_time,
  -- engagement_time_msec: try to extract from event_params where key='engagement_time_msec' as int (milliseconds)
  (SELECT
     COALESCE(
       CAST(ep.value.int_value AS INT64),
       SAFE_CAST(ep.value.string_value AS INT64)
     )
   FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS ep
   WHERE ep.key = 'engagement_time_msec'
   LIMIT 1) AS engagement_time_msec,
  -- windows: mark membership. Lift literal window bounds out of view (user can filter _TABLE_SUFFIX and timestamps outside)
  -- Here we mark events whose event_timestamp falls within the last 7 days or last 2 days relative to a reference_timestamp placeholder.
  -- The view leaves reference_timestamp as NULL; users should supply a filter/replace when querying the view.
  FALSE AS in_7d_window,
  FALSE AS in_2d_window
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20201101' AND '20210131'
events_in_windows.description: Select all raw event rows that fall within either the 7-day window or the 2-day window, retaining event timestamp, pseudo user id, and engagement time fields (both engagement_time and engagement_time_msec if present). Do not aggregate yet; mark which window(s) each event belongs to (a single event may belong to both windows if timestamps overlap).

normalize_engagement_time.name: normalize_engagement_time
normalize_engagement_time.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a stable event identifier (use event_timestamp combined with pseudo_user to form event_id if events_in_windows provides event_id)
  eiw.event_id AS event_id,
  eiw.pseudo_user AS pseudo_user,
  eiw.event_timestamp AS event_timestamp,
  -- Normalize engagement_time:
  -- Prefer engagement_time (string) parsed as numeric seconds when present; otherwise use engagement_time_msec / 1000.
  -- If both are NULL, preserve NULL (do not collapse rows). Do not coerce NULLs to zero here to preserve information.
  CASE
    WHEN eiw.engagement_time IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(eiw.engagement_time AS FLOAT64)
    WHEN eiw.engagement_time_msec IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(CAST(eiw.engagement_time_msec AS FLOAT64), 1000.0)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS engagement_time_seconds,
  eiw.in_7d_window AS in_7d_window,
  eiw.in_2d_window AS in_2d_window
FROM `events_in_windows` AS eiw
normalize_engagement_time.description: Normalize/derive a single engagement_time_seconds value per event: prefer engagement_time if present, otherwise convert engagement_time_msec to seconds; handle NULLs as zero or NULL consistently (do not collapse rows). Preserve indicators of which window the event is in (from events_in_windows).

candidate_customer_line_items.name: candidate_customer_line_items
candidate_customer_line_items.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(s.visitorId AS STRING) AS customer_id,
  h.transaction.transactionId AS order_id,
  CONCAT(CAST(s.visitId AS STRING), '-', CAST(h.hitNumber AS STRING), '-', COALESCE(p.productSKU, '')) AS line_id,
  NULLIF(p.v2ProductName, '') AS product_id,
  p.productSKU AS product_sku,
  p.v2ProductName AS product_name,
  COALESCE(p.productQuantity, 0) AS quantity,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) AS event_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS s,
UNNEST(s.hits) AS h,
UNNEST(h.product) AS p
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170701' AND '20170731'
  -- only include rows that are actual purchases (have a transaction id)
  AND h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
  -- restrict to customers who bought the target product: lift actual list of customer ids out of the view;
  -- here we include all customers (placeholder) — consumers of this view should JOIN/WHERE using customers_who_bought_target.
  -- exclude the target product by product name — lift the actual target name out of the view as a parameter when querying.
  AND TRUE
  -- exclude product rows where product name equals the target (to be supplied at query time), e.g.:
  -- AND p.v2ProductName <> 'TARGET PRODUCT NAME'
candidate_customer_line_items.description: All July 2017 line items restricted to customers identified in customers_who_bought_target, excluding line items for the target product name (these are the candidate products to aggregate).

sessions_2017.name: sessions_2017
sessions_2017.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "-", CAST(visitStartTime AS STRING)) AS session_id,
  `date` AS date,
  -- expose a single representative traffic_source string; callers can choose campaign/medium/source as needed
  COALESCE(trafficSource.campaign, trafficSource.source, trafficSource.medium) AS traffic_source,
  totals.transactionRevenue AS transaction_revenue_raw
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20171231'
sessions_2017.description: Filter the raw sessions to include only sessions whose date falls within calendar year 2017.

feb_sessions_and_hits_with_transactions.name: feb_sessions_and_hits_with_transactions
feb_sessions_and_hits_with_transactions.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(CAST(s.visitorId AS STRING)) AS fullVisitorId,
  s.date AS session_date,
  -- session-level transaction id: GA stores totals.transactions as a count, not an id.
  -- Keep the count (nullable) as the session_transaction_id per instructions to "keep indicators/ids".
  NULLIF(CAST(s.totals.transactions AS STRING), 'NULL') AS session_transaction_id,
  s.totals.transactionRevenue AS session_transaction_revenue,
  -- hit-level transaction id and revenue from unnested hits
  h.transaction.transactionId AS hit_transaction_id,
  h.transaction.transactionRevenue AS hit_transaction_revenue,
  s.device.deviceCategory AS device_category,
  CONCAT(CAST(s.visitId AS STRING)) AS session_id,
  h.hitNumber AS hit_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS s,
UNNEST(s.hits) AS h
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170201' AND '20170228'
  AND (
    -- session-level indicator (either transaction count or revenue present)
    s.totals.transactionRevenue IS NOT NULL
    OR s.totals.transactions IS NOT NULL
    -- OR hit-level transaction present
    OR h.transaction.transactionRevenue IS NOT NULL
    OR h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
  )
grain: row_per_session_or_hit_event (one row per hit within sessions that have a session- or hit-level transaction in Feb 2017)
feb_sessions_and_hits_with_transactions.description: Select all session-level and hit-level events for February 2017 (2017-02-01 through 2017-02-28 inclusive), keep indicators/ids that identify a transaction at either session level or hit level and include device category and session date. This relation is one row per relevant session or hit event (whichever row grain you choose later) that can show a transaction during Feb 2017.

visitor_first_visit_in_feb.name: visitor_first_visit_in_feb
visitor_first_visit_in_feb.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fullVisitorId`,
  MIN(PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', `date`)) AS `first_visit_date_in_feb_2017`
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170201' AND '20170228'
  AND SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', `date`) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `fullVisitorId`
visitor_first_visit_in_feb.description: For each visitor (fullVisitorId) compute the earliest session_date in February 2017 (their first visit date in Feb). One row per visitor who had any session in February.

visitor_first_transaction_in_feb.name: visitor_first_transaction_in_feb
visitor_first_transaction_in_feb.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  MIN(s.date) AS first_transaction_date_in_feb_2017
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS s,
  UNNEST(s.hits) AS h
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170201' AND '20170228'
  AND (
    -- session-level transaction revenue (session totals)
    (s.totals.transactionRevenue IS NOT NULL AND s.totals.transactionRevenue > 0)
    -- hit-level explicit transaction id
    OR (h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL)
    -- hit-level transaction revenue
    OR (h.transaction.transactionRevenue IS NOT NULL AND h.transaction.transactionRevenue > 0)
  )
GROUP BY
  s.fullVisitorId
visitor_first_transaction_in_feb.description: For each visitor (fullVisitorId) identify the earliest date in February 2017 on which the visitor had at least one transaction (transaction indicated by session-level or hit-level transaction id or non-null transaction revenue). One row per visitor who had at least one transaction in Feb.

sessions_date_filtered.name: sessions_date_filtered
sessions_date_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- session identifier: use visitId (unique per session) combined with visitStartTime to ensure uniqueness across shards
  CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "-", CAST(visitStartTime AS STRING)) AS session_id,
  -- session date as recorded in the GA shard
  `date` AS session_date,
  -- session-level number of transactions (can be NULL)
  totals.transactions AS transactions,
  -- session-level reported transaction revenue (in micros / integer) (can be NULL)
  totals.transactionRevenue AS productRevenue,
  -- session-level pageviews (can be NULL)
  totals.pageviews AS pageviews,
  -- visitor identifier from the session (may be NULL)
  visitorId AS visitors
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170401' AND '20170731'
sessions_date_filtered.description: Select sessions whose session date falls in the target inclusive range (2017-04-01 to 2017-07-31). Keep all session-level columns needed for classification and metrics (session identifier, session_date, transactions, productRevenue, pageviews, visitors).

july_2017_purchases.name: july_2017_purchases
july_2017_purchases.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(h.transaction.transactionId, CAST(h.transaction.transactionId AS STRING)) AS purchase_id,
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  COALESCE(p.productSKU, p.v2ProductName) AS product_id,
  p.v2ProductName AS product_name,
  p.productQuantity AS quantity,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', _TABLE_SUFFIX) AS purchase_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS h,
  UNNEST(h.product) AS p
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170701' AND '20170731'
  AND h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
july_2017_purchases.description: All purchase events (order lines or purchase records) that occurred in July 2017 with their visitor identifier, product identifier, product name, and quantity.

candidate_purchases_by_qualifying_visito.name: candidate_purchases_by_qualifying_visitors
candidate_purchases_by_qualifying_visito.body_sql:
SELECT
  h.transaction.transactionId AS purchase_id,
  t.visitorId AS visitor_id,
  p.productSKU AS product_id,
  p.v2ProductName AS product_name,
  p.productQuantity AS quantity
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS t,
UNNEST(t.hits) AS h,
UNNEST(h.product) AS p
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170701' AND '20170731'
  AND h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
  -- restrict to visitors who purchased any YouTube-related product in July 2017
  AND t.visitorId IN (
    SELECT DISTINCT t2.visitorId
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS t2,
    UNNEST(t2.hits) AS h2,
    UNNEST(h2.product) AS p2
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170701' AND '20170731'
      AND h2.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
      AND LOWER(IFNULL(p2.v2ProductName, '')) LIKE '%youtube%'
  )
candidate_purchases_by_qualifying_visito.description: All July 2017 purchase rows restricted to only those made by visitors identified as having bought a YouTube-related product; retains product_name and quantity for each purchase row.

sessions_jan2017_campaign_visitors.name: sessions_jan2017_campaign_visitors
sessions_jan2017_campaign_visitors.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(visitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  CAST(visitId AS STRING) AS session_id,
  CAST(h.hitNumber AS STRING) AS hit_id,
  date AS event_date,
  h.time AS event_timestamp,
  trafficSource.campaign AS campaign
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
UNNEST(hits) AS h
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170131'
  AND trafficSource.campaign IS NOT NULL
  AND LOWER(trafficSource.campaign) LIKE '%data share%'
  AND (h.type = 'EVENT' OR h.eventInfo IS NOT NULL)
sessions_jan2017_campaign_visitors.description: Select sessions in January 2017 for visitors whose campaign name contains the substring 'Data Share'. Produce one row per session-hit (event) including session id, visitor id, event/hit id, event timestamp/date, campaign name. This is the cohort of interest constrained by date and campaign.

records_2014.name: records_2014
records_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  drg_definition,
  provider_city AS city,
  total_discharges,
  average_total_payments AS total_payments,
  provider_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
grain: one row per record (one input row from the 2014 inpatient_charges shard)
records_2014.description: Subset of the dataset restricted to year 2014, keeping fields needed for DRG, city, total discharges, and total payments (no aggregation).

discharges_payments_by_drg_city_provider.name: discharges_payments_by_drg_city_provider
discharges_payments_by_drg_city_provider.body_sql:
SELECT
  ic.drg_definition AS drg_definition,
  ic.provider_city AS city,
  ic.provider_id AS provider_id,
  SUM(ic.total_discharges) AS sum_total_discharges,
  SUM(ic.average_total_payments * ic.total_discharges) AS sum_total_payments
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*` AS ic
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @shard_start_year AND @shard_end_year
GROUP BY
  ic.drg_definition,
  ic.provider_city,
  ic.provider_id
discharges_payments_by_drg_city_provider.description: Aggregate total discharges and total payments at the finest reporting unit required for later grouping: sum totals per DRG definition, city, and provider (keeps provider-level rows so city sums can be derived without losing provider detail).

total_discharges_by_drg.name: total_discharges_by_drg
total_discharges_by_drg.body_sql:
SELECT
  ic.drg_definition AS drg_definition,
  SUM(ic.total_discharges) AS drg_total_discharges
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*` AS ic
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
  AND ic.drg_definition IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  ic.drg_definition
total_discharges_by_drg.description: Compute total discharges per DRG definition across all cities and providers by summing the provider-level aggregates (identifies the DRG with maximum total discharges).

prescriptions_2014.name: prescriptions_2014
prescriptions_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.drug_exposure_id AS prescription_id,
  loc.state AS state_name,
  de.drug_concept_id AS medication_id,
  c.concept_name AS medication_name,
  de.drug_exposure_start_date AS prescription_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` AS de
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.location` AS loc
ON
  de.provider_id = loc.location_id
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS c
ON
  de.drug_concept_id = c.concept_id
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM de.drug_exposure_start_date) = 2014
  AND loc.state IS NOT NULL
  AND LENGTH(loc.state) = 2
  AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(UPPER(loc.state), r'^[A-Z]{2}$')
prescriptions_2014.description: All prescription records restricted to the year 2014 and to U.S. states (exclude territories).

med_state_rank.name: med_state_rank
med_state_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  nppes_provider_state AS state_name,
  -- Use drug_name as medication_name and medication_id is the drug_name (no separate ID in source).
  drug_name AS medication_name,
  -- Carry medication_id as drug_name to keep joinable at the required grain (one row per state + medication_id).
  drug_name AS medication_id,
  -- prescription_count: total claims for this drug in the state (lifted literal: YEAR not embedded)
  SUM(total_claim_count) AS prescription_count,
  -- Rank medications within each state by prescription_count (highest = 1)
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY nppes_provider_state ORDER BY SUM(total_claim_count) DESC) AS med_rank
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
GROUP BY
  nppes_provider_state,
  drug_name
med_state_rank.description: Rank medications within each state by their 2014 prescription_count (highest = rank 1).

top_medication_per_state.name: top_medication_per_state
top_medication_per_state.body_sql:
SELECT
  nppes_provider_state AS state_name,
  drug_name AS medication_name,
  SUM(total_claim_count) AS prescription_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
GROUP BY nppes_provider_state, drug_name
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY nppes_provider_state ORDER BY SUM(total_claim_count) DESC) = 1
ORDER BY state_name
top_medication_per_state.description: Select one medication per state where the rank equals 1 (ties arbitrarily resolved); orderable by state_name in final output.

provider_services_2014.name: provider_services_2014
provider_services_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- provider identifier (kept for joinability)
  provider_id,
  -- service type: 'outpatient' or 'inpatient'
  service_type,
  -- cost measure for the service record (average total payments)
  cost,
  -- year literal lifted out of view definition (2014)
  2014 AS year
FROM (
  -- outpatient service records for 2014
  SELECT
    provider_id,
    'outpatient' AS service_type,
    average_total_payments AS cost,
    CONCAT(CAST(provider_id AS STRING), '-', COALESCE(apc, '')) AS service_record_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'

  UNION ALL

  -- inpatient service records for 2014
  SELECT
    provider_id,
    'inpatient' AS service_type,
    average_total_payments AS cost,
    CONCAT(CAST(provider_id AS STRING), '-', COALESCE(drg_definition, '')) AS service_record_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
)
provider_services_2014.description: Select all service cost records for the year 2014, keeping service type (outpatient vs inpatient), provider identifier, and the cost measure for each record.

provider_service_costs_clean.name: provider_service_costs_clean
provider_service_costs_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key so view is joinable; outpatient and inpatient use provider_id, physicians use npi (kept under provider_id)
  COALESCE(o.provider_id, i.provider_id, p.npi) AS provider_id,
  -- canonicalize service type to exactly 'outpatient' or 'inpatient'
  CASE
    WHEN o.provider_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'outpatient'
    WHEN i.provider_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'inpatient'
    WHEN p.npi IS NOT NULL THEN 'outpatient'  -- physicians/suppliers are ambulatory/outpatient-like by nature in these tables
    ELSE NULL
  END AS service_type_canonical,
  -- normalize/cast various cost fields into a single numeric cost; prefer most-representative fields per source
  CASE
    WHEN o.provider_id IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(o.average_estimated_submitted_charges AS FLOAT64)
    WHEN i.provider_id IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(i.average_total_payments AS FLOAT64)
    WHEN p.npi IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(p.average_medicare_allowed_amt AS FLOAT64)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS cost_numeric
FROM
  -- outpatient wildcard across 2011-2015; lift suffix range out of view (caller should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX)
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*` AS o
  LEFT JOIN
  -- inpatient wildcard across 2011-2015; join is lateral-like by provider and DRG/APC not required here — keep rows separate via COALESCE logic
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*` AS i
  ON FALSE  -- keep disjoint rows; we want one row per service record coming from whichever table; joining would multiply rows
  LEFT JOIN
  -- physicians/suppliers wildcard across 2012-2015
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*` AS p
  ON FALSE
WHERE
  1 = 1
  -- NOTE: This view is designed to be used with a caller-applied _TABLE_SUFFIX filter on each wildcard table.
  -- Example filters the caller should apply: o._TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015', i._TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015', p._TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2012' AND '2015'
provider_service_costs_clean.description: Normalize and canonicalize the cost values and service_type labels, converting/casting costs to numeric and mapping service type variants to two canonical values: 'outpatient' and 'inpatient'.

avg_cost_per_provider_service.name: avg_cost_per_provider_service
avg_cost_per_provider_service.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key so view is joinable
  provider_id,
  -- canonical service type: 'outpatient' for outpatient tables, 'inpatient' for inpatient tables
  service_type_canonical,
  -- average cost per provider per service type in 2014 (lift literal '2014' out of view usage via _TABLE_SUFFIX filter)
  AVG(avg_payment) AS avg_cost
FROM (
  -- outpatient source: use wildcard and restrict to 2014 shards; average_total_payments represents cost per service row
  SELECT
    provider_id,
    'outpatient' AS service_type_canonical,
    CAST(average_total_payments AS FLOAT64) AS avg_payment
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
    AND average_total_payments IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  -- inpatient source: use wildcard and restrict to 2014 shards; average_total_payments represents cost per DRG row
  SELECT
    provider_id,
    'inpatient' AS service_type_canonical,
    CAST(average_total_payments AS FLOAT64) AS avg_payment
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
    AND average_total_payments IS NOT NULL
)
GROUP BY
  provider_id,
  service_type_canonical
avg_cost_per_provider_service.description: Compute the average cost per provider for each canonical service type (outpatient and inpatient) within 2014.

records_with_contributions.name: records_with_contributions
records_with_contributions.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- provider identifier (kept so view is joinable). For inpatient rows it's provider_id; for outpatient rows npi is aliased to provider_id.
  provider_id,
  -- calendar year taken from shard suffix so view can be queried across years
  calendar_year,
  -- inpatient contribution: NULL if either component NULL
  CASE
    WHEN average_medicare_payments IS NULL OR total_discharges IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE average_medicare_payments * total_discharges
  END AS inpatient_contribution,
  -- outpatient contribution: NULL if either component NULL
  CASE
    WHEN average_medicare_payment_amt IS NULL OR line_srvc_cnt IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE average_medicare_payment_amt * line_srvc_cnt
  END AS outpatient_contribution
FROM (
  -- Union inpatient shards and outpatient (physicians) shards into one per-row set.
  -- Inpatient shards: years 2011-2015 (use wildcard and _TABLE_SUFFIX filter)
  SELECT
    `provider_id` AS provider_id,
    _TABLE_SUFFIX AS calendar_year,
    average_medicare_payments,
    total_discharges,
    -- these columns not present in inpatient shards; keep NULL so union aligns
    NULL AS average_medicare_payment_amt,
    NULL AS line_srvc_cnt
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'

  UNION ALL

  -- Outpatient (physicians_and_other_supplier) shards: years 2012-2015
  SELECT
    `npi` AS provider_id,
    _TABLE_SUFFIX AS calendar_year,
    -- inpatient columns not present in physicians table; keep NULL so union aligns
    NULL AS average_medicare_payments,
    NULL AS total_discharges,
    -- outpatient contribution inputs
    `average_medicare_payment_amt`,
    `line_srvc_cnt`
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2012' AND '2015'
)
grain: one row per original source record (union of inpatient and outpatient rows)
records_with_contributions.description: Compute per-record numeric contributions: inpatient_contribution = average_medicare_payments * total_discharges (NULL if either input NULL) and outpatient_contribution = average_total_payments * outpatient_services (NULL if either input NULL). Preserve provider and calendar_year.

provider_total_inpatient_2011_2015.name: provider_total_inpatient_2011_2015
provider_total_inpatient_2011_2015.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  SUM(average_total_payments) AS total_inpatient_2011_2015
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
  AND average_total_payments IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  provider_id
provider_total_inpatient_2011_2015.description: For each provider, sum inpatient_contribution across all their records in 2011–2015 (ignore records where inpatient_contribution is NULL). This produces one row per provider with their total inpatient cost over the five-year span.

person_cohort.name: person_cohort
person_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  CAST(person_id AS INT64) AS person_id
FROM (
  -- patients from OMOP person table
  SELECT person_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person`

  UNION ALL

  -- referring providers/beneficiaries from Medicare DME shards (string NPIs may represent persons/providers)
  SELECT SAFE_CAST(referring_npi AS INT64) AS person_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.referring_durable_medical_equip_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2013' AND '2014'

  UNION ALL

  -- persons appearing in dose_era (medication exposures)
  SELECT person_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.dose_era`
)
WHERE person_id IS NOT NULL
person_cohort.description: All distinct persons in the dataset (the study population) to define the denominator; one row per person id.

icd10_top_level_concepts.name: icd10_top_level_concepts
icd10_top_level_concepts.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.concept_id AS top_concept_id,
  c.concept_code AS condition_standard_code,
  c.concept_name AS condition_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS c
WHERE
  -- lift literals: top-level ICD-10-CM codes of interest (L70, L20, L40, L80)
  c.concept_code IN ('L70', 'L20', 'L40', 'L80')
  AND c.domain_id = 'Condition'
  AND c.vocabulary_id LIKE 'ICD10%'  -- ensure ICD-10 family vocabulary
  AND c.standard_concept = 'S'
icd10_top_level_concepts.description: The four ICD-10-CM top-level standard concepts of interest (logical rows representing the canonical standard concept ids/codes for L70, L20, L40, L80) with their plain names; one row per top-level condition concept.

condition_concept_descendants.name: condition_concept_descendants
condition_concept_descendants.body_sql:
SELECT
  top_c.concept_id AS top_concept_id,
  desc_c.concept_id AS descendant_concept_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS top_c
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_relationship` AS rel
  ON rel.concept_id_1 = top_c.concept_id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS desc_c
  ON desc_c.concept_id = rel.concept_id_2
WHERE
  -- top-level ICD-10-CM concepts: vocabulary_id = 'ICD10CM' and standard concepts (standard_concept = 'S')
  top_c.vocabulary_id = 'ICD10CM'
  AND top_c.standard_concept = 'S'
  -- include only descendant concepts that are standard (so they are usable as condition concepts)
  AND desc_c.standard_concept = 'S'
condition_concept_descendants.description: All descendant standard concepts (via concept relationship hierarchy) for each top-level ICD-10-CM concept, producing rows that map each descendant (including the top-level concept itself) to its top-level condition concept.

person_condition_flag.name: person_condition_flag
person_condition_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.person_id AS person_id,
  top.concept_id AS top_concept_id,
  -- flag true if person has any condition mapped to a descendant of the top-level concept
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.condition_occurrence` co
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca
      ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
    WHERE co.person_id = p.person_id
      AND ca.ancestor_concept_id = top.concept_id
  ) AS has_condition_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` p
CROSS JOIN
  -- top-level concepts: restrict to standard top-level concepts by domain if desired;
  -- here we take concepts that are their own ancestor (level 0) as top-level candidates.
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` top
WHERE
  -- liftable literal: treat top concepts as those that have descendants (including themselves)
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca2
    WHERE ca2.ancestor_concept_id = top.concept_id
  )
person_condition_flag.description: For each person and each top-level condition, a row for persons who have at least one clinical record mapped to any descendant standard concept of that top-level concept; includes one boolean/flag per person-top_concept indicating presence (de-duplicated to at most one row per person per top-level condition).

all_participants_cohort.name: all_participants_cohort
all_participants_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(person_id AS STRING) AS participant_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person`
all_participants_cohort.description: All participants in the dataset (base cohort). Do not apply additional study filters; retain participant identifier and any metadata needed to join to medication records.

normalized_medication_rxcui.name: normalized_medication_rxcui
normalized_medication_rxcui.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.person_id AS participant_id,
  de.drug_exposure_id AS medication_record_id,
  -- normalize rxcui from drug_source_value if numeric; leave NULL otherwise
  SAFE_CAST(TRIM(de.drug_source_value) AS INT64) AS rxcui_int,
  -- flag for RxCUI == 35208 (quinapril) after integer-cast normalization
  SAFE_CAST(TRIM(de.drug_source_value) AS INT64) = 35208 AS is_quinapril_rxcui,
  -- explicit 'no medications' indicators: common textual phrases in source value (case-insensitive)
  (
    LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(de.drug_source_value, ''))) IN ('no medication', 'no medications', 'none', 'n/a', 'na', 'not medicated')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(COALESCE(de.drug_source_value, '')), r'^(no med(ic)?(ation)?s?$|none$|n/?a$|not medicated)')
  ) AS is_explicit_no_medications,
  -- missing medication data: null/empty drug_source_value and no drug_concept_id and no drug_exposure dates
  (
    (de.drug_source_value IS NULL OR TRIM(de.drug_source_value) = '')
    AND de.drug_concept_id IS NULL
    AND de.drug_exposure_start_date IS NULL
    AND de.drug_exposure_end_date IS NULL
  ) AS is_missing_medication_data
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` de
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` p
ON de.person_id = p.person_id
normalized_medication_rxcui.description: Normalize and canonicalize medication RxCUI values: cast to integer where possible, trim/clean text, and set explicit flags for (a) records with RxCUI = 35208, (b) records explicitly indicating 'no medications', and (c) truly missing/unknown medication data.

participant_quinapril_usage_flags.name: participant_quinapril_usage_flags
participant_quinapril_usage_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- participant identifier
  p.person_id AS participant_id,
  -- whether participant has any drug_exposure with RxCUI 35208
  EXISTS(
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` de
    WHERE de.person_id = p.person_id
      -- lift RxCUI literal out of view: compare to the RxCUI value 35208
      AND CAST(de.drug_source_concept_id AS INT64) = 35208
  ) AS has_quinapril_rxcui,
  -- explicit 'no medications' indication:
  -- interpret as a person having a drug_exposure record with drug_source_value explicitly equal to 'NO MEDICATIONS' (case-insensitive)
  EXISTS(
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` de2
    WHERE de2.person_id = p.person_id
      AND LOWER(COALESCE(de2.drug_source_value, '')) = 'no medications'
  ) AS has_explicit_no_medications,
  -- missing medication data: person has no drug_exposure records at all OR all drug_exposure rows for them are NULL/empty for identifying fields
  (
    NOT EXISTS(
      SELECT 1
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` de3
      WHERE de3.person_id = p.person_id
    )
    OR NOT EXISTS(
      -- check for any non-null meaningful medication info for this person
      SELECT 1
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` de4
      WHERE de4.person_id = p.person_id
        AND (
          de4.drug_concept_id IS NOT NULL
          OR de4.drug_source_value IS NOT NULL
          OR de4.drug_source_concept_id IS NOT NULL
          OR de4.drug_exposure_start_date IS NOT NULL
        )
    )
  ) AS has_missing_medication_data
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` p
participant_quinapril_usage_flags.description: One row per participant indicating whether they have any medication record with RxCUI = 35208, whether they have an explicit 'no medications' indication, and whether medication data is wholly missing/unknown (so they should be excluded).

track_points_sel.name: track_points_sel
track_points_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid AS storm_id,
  name AS storm_name,
  iso_time AS point_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  basin
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
WHERE basin = 'NA'
  AND iso_time IS NOT NULL
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
  -- keep only storms that have at least one point in 2020
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes` h2
    WHERE h2.sid = `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`.sid
      AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM h2.iso_time) = 2020
  )
track_points_sel.description: Select all track point records for storms, keeping timestamped coordinates, storm identifier/name, basin, and any fields needed to order points in time. Filter to points that belong to storms which have at least one point in the year 2020 and that are located in the North Atlantic basin (basin membership can be per-point or per-storm depending on schema). Also exclude points with missing/invalid coordinates.

atlantic_2020_observations.name: atlantic_2020_observations
atlantic_2020_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid AS storm_id,
  iso_time AS observation_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  usa_wind AS sustained_wind
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
WHERE
  basin = 'NA'
  AND season = '2020'
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND iso_time IS NOT NULL
atlantic_2020_observations.description: Select all observation records for the North Atlantic basin during the 2020 season, excluding observations with NULL or missing coordinates. Keep observation timestamp/sequence, lat/lon, storm identifier, and sustained wind at each observation.

storm_events_filtered_years.name: storm_events_filtered_years
storm_events_filtered_years.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_id,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TIMESTAMP(event_begin_time)) AS event_year,
  state AS state_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.storms_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1950' AND '2024'
  AND event_type IN ('Tornado','Hail','Thunderstorm Wind','Flood','Flash Flood','High Wind','Lightning','Snow','Winter Storm','Hurricane','Tropical Storm','Waterspout','Marine Thunderstorm','Coastal Flood')

semantic_filters.event_type: is a storm type (exclude non-storm types)

storm_events_filtered_years.description: Select storm event records restricted to the target year range and to storm-type events only (exclude non-storm event types). Keep one row per original event record with its event year and state identifier.

station_cohort_by_period_of_record.name: station_cohort_by_period_of_record
station_cohort_by_period_of_record.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(s.usaf, '-', s.wban) AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', SAFE_CAST(CONCAT(SUBSTR(s.begin,1,4), SUBSTR(s.begin,6,2), SUBSTR(s.begin,9,2)) AS STRING)) AS period_of_record_start_date,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', SAFE_CAST(CONCAT(SUBSTR(s.`end`,1,4), SUBSTR(s.`end`,6,2), SUBSTR(s.`end`,9,2)) AS STRING)) AS period_of_record_end_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` s
WHERE
  -- require parsed start <= 2000-01-01 and parsed end >= 2019-06-30
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', SAFE_CAST(CONCAT(SUBSTR(s.begin,1,4), SUBSTR(s.begin,6,2), SUBSTR(s.begin,9,2)) AS STRING)) <= DATE '2000-01-01'
  AND PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', SAFE_CAST(CONCAT(SUBSTR(s.`end`,1,4), SUBSTR(s.`end`,6,2), SUBSTR(s.`end`,9,2)) AS STRING)) >= DATE '2019-06-30'
station_cohort_by_period_of_record.description: Select stations whose period-of-record covers the required range: start_date on or before 2000-01-01 and end_date on or after 2019-06-30. This yields the candidate station set to evaluate for 2019 completeness.

daily_observations_2019.name: daily_observations_2019
daily_observations_2019.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stn, IFNULL(CONCAT('-', wban), '')) AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS obs_date,
  NULLIF(temp, 9999.9) AS temp,
  NULLIF(max, 9999.9) AS max_temp,
  NULLIF(min, 9999.9) AS min_temp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2019' AND '2019'
  AND -- restrict to calendar year 2019 (redundant with _TABLE_SUFFIX but keeps intent clear)
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) BETWEEN DATE '2019-01-01' AND DATE '2019-12-31'
daily_observations_2019.description: All daily observation records restricted to calendar dates in 2019 (2019-01-01 through 2019-12-31) with raw temp, max, and min fields (no aggregation). Keep original nulls so validity can be computed later.

station_observations_raw.name: station_observations_raw
station_observations_raw.body_sql:
-- View body: select raw observation records for a station on June 12 in years 2011..2020 (local date).
-- Lifted literals: target month=6, target day=12, start_year=2011, end_year=2020.
SELECT
  CONCAT(COALESCE(stn, ''), COALESCE(wban, '')) AS station_id,    -- keep key/id
  PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS obs_timestamp,
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  CAST(mo AS INT64) AS month,
  CAST(da AS INT64) AS day,
  -- temperature in dataset is Fahrenheit mean for the day; keep as-is
  CASE WHEN temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE temp END AS temperature,
  -- mean wind speed (wdsp) stored as string in some shards; coerce to float and treat 999.9 as NULL
  NULLIF(CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '') AS FLOAT64), 999.9) AS wind_speed,
  -- precipitation in inches; 99.99 denotes missing
  CASE WHEN prcp = 99.99 THEN NULL ELSE prcp END AS precipitation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) BETWEEN 2011 AND 2020
  AND CAST(mo AS INT64) = 6
  AND CAST(da AS INT64) = 12
  -- restrict wildcard suffix to the years of interest for performance (gsod tables are named by year)
  AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2020'
station_observations_raw.description: Select all raw observation records for the specified station and calendar date range (years in 2011..2020) but do not aggregate. Keep observations that occur on June 12 of any year at the station (local date).

source_tables_cohort.name: source_tables_cohort
source_tables_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS source_table,
  latitude AS latitude_raw,
  longitude AS longitude_raw,
  -- compose a DATE from year, month, day; keep NULLs if components missing
  SAFE_CAST(CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING),2,'0')) AS DATE) AS date_raw,
  wind_speed AS daily_average_wind_speed_raw,
  -- row identifier to preserve grain (one row per source_table, row_id)
  -- use CONCAT of _TABLE_SUFFIX and the row's OFFSET-like surrogate: use GENERATE_UUID() is non-deterministic
  -- instead create a deterministic row_id from available columns: year/month/day/hour/latitude/longitude and CAST of wind_speed
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '|',
         COALESCE(CAST(year AS STRING),''), '|',
         COALESCE(CAST(month AS STRING),''), '|',
         COALESCE(CAST(day AS STRING),''), '|',
         COALESCE(CAST(hour AS STRING),''), '|',
         COALESCE(CAST(latitude AS STRING),''), '|',
         COALESCE(CAST(longitude AS STRING),''), '|',
         COALESCE(CAST(wind_speed AS STRING),'')) AS row_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
WHERE
  -- select only tables whose name begins with the literal prefix 'icoads_core'
  STARTS_WITH(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '')  -- wildcard metadata available; keep this no-op to show intent
  AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @table_suffix_start AND @table_suffix_end
source_tables_cohort.description: Select rows from all source tables whose table name starts with the literal prefix 'icoads_core' and that lie within the requested date range; keep raw latitude, longitude, date, and the raw daily-average-wind-speed column (unnormalized). This is a coarse row-level filter (table-level + date range) but does not apply NULL-exclusion for wind speed yet.

normalize_columns.name: normalize_columns
normalize_columns.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- identify source table exactly as in DDL
  '`bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`' AS source_table,
  -- keep original key/grain: use stn || '-' || wban || '-' || year || '-' || mo || '-' || da as row id
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban, '-', year, '-', mo, '-', da) AS row_id,
  -- normalize latitude/longitude from stations join when available, otherwise NULL
  -- stations table has usaf/wban; gsod stn column corresponds to usaf and wban combination in stations
  -- but because matching can be ambiguous, prefer NULL when not joinable; keep numeric types
  NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(NULL AS STRING)), '') AS latitude,
  NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(NULL AS STRING)), '') AS longitude,
  -- compose date from year/mo/da fields (gsod uses strings); cast safely to DATE, return NULL on failure
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(CAST(mo AS STRING) AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(CAST(da AS STRING) AS STRING),2,'0'))) AS date,
  -- daily_average_wind_speed: gsod.wdsp is mean wind in knots (string), 999.9 = missing -> canonicalize to NULL, cast to NUMERIC
  (CASE
    WHEN wdsp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(wdsp) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '999.9') AS NUMERIC)
  END) AS daily_average_wind_speed
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- keep shards selectable by caller; lift date range literals out of the view by allowing all rows here
  TRUE
normalize_columns.description: Normalize and cast the raw columns from the selected source rows into canonical output names and types: latitude (numeric), longitude (numeric), date (date), daily_average_wind_speed (numeric). Also handle any simple cleaning (trim, NULL canonicalization). Keeps one row per original row.

stations_cohort.name: stations_cohort
stations_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  usaf AS usaf,
  NULL AS station_id_optional
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`
WHERE
  usaf IS NOT NULL
  AND usaf != '999999'
GROUP BY
  usaf
stations_cohort.description: All distinct weather stations that have a non-null USAF identifier and USAF != '999999'. This defines the universe of stations to consider.

daily_valid_flags.name: daily_valid_flags
daily_valid_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.usaf AS usaf,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(g.year, LPAD(g.mo,2,'0'), LPAD(g.da,2,'0'))) AS obs_date,
  -- temp, max, min valid when present (not NULL) and not equal to sentinel 9999.9
  (g.temp IS NOT NULL AND g.temp <> 9999.9) AS temp_valid,
  (g.max IS NOT NULL AND g.max <> 9999.9) AS max_valid,
  (g.min IS NOT NULL AND g.min <> 9999.9) AS min_valid
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS g
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
ON
  g.stn = s.usaf AND g.wban = s.wban
WHERE
  -- limit to calendar year 2022 using the shard suffix and year column
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2022'
  AND SAFE_CAST(g.year AS INT64) = 2022

semantic_filters.value_filters_note: flags mark (value IS NOT NULL AND value != 9999.9) but rows are not dropped here

daily_valid_flags.description: Daily observations for calendar year 2022 with flags indicating whether temperature, maximum, and minimum values are present and not equal to the invalid sentinel 9999.9. One row per station-day within 2022.

station_day_validity.name: station_day_validity
station_day_validity.body_sql:
SELECT
  stn AS usaf,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS obs_date,
  -- all_metrics_valid: true if temp, max, and min are present and not equal to the GSOD missing sentinels (9999.9)
  (SAFE_CAST(temp AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(max AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(min AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
   AND temp != 9999.9 AND max != 9999.9 AND min != 9999.9) AS all_metrics_valid
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
station_day_validity.description: Per station-day summary indicating whether that day has all three valid metrics (temperature, maximum, minimum). One row per station-day, with a boolean or integer flag all_metrics_valid.

stations_in_washington.name: stations_in_washington
stations_in_washington.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- station_id: canonicalized from available station identifiers in the stations table
  -- prefer 'usaf' if present, else use concat(usaf,'-',wban) if both present, else use 'call' as fallback
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(s.usaf) IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.usaf) <> '' THEN TRIM(s.usaf)
    WHEN TRIM(s.usaf) IS NULL OR TRIM(s.usaf) = '' AND TRIM(s.wban) IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.wban) <> '' THEN CONCAT(TRIM(s.usaf),'-',TRIM(s.wban))
    WHEN (TRIM(s.usaf) IS NULL OR TRIM(s.usaf) = '') AND (TRIM(s.wban) IS NULL OR TRIM(s.wban) = '') AND TRIM(s.call) IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.call) <> '' THEN TRIM(s.call)
    ELSE CONCAT('station_', CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER () AS STRING))
  END AS station_id,
  s.name AS station_name,
  -- canonicalize state field: stations table uses 'state' already; normalize to two-letter uppercase if available
  UPPER(TRIM(COALESCE(s.state, ''))) AS state
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
WHERE
  -- restrict to stations located in Washington State
  -- accept common representations: 'WA', 'Wa', 'wa', 'Washington'
  UPPER(TRIM(COALESCE(s.state, ''))) IN ('WA', 'WASHINGTON')
  -- ensure station metadata exists (table row exists), so only valid stations are returned
stations_in_washington.description: Select weather station identifiers and their state/location fields restricted to stations located in Washington State (canonicalize whatever state identifier field the schema uses). Only include stations that are considered valid stations (exist in station metadata).

daily_precip_records.name: daily_precip_records
daily_precip_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  `stn` AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d',
    CONCAT(CAST(`year` AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(`mo` AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(`da` AS STRING),2,'0'))
  ) AS observation_date,
  -- convert inches to millimeters (1 inch = 25.4 mm)
  SAFE_CAST(`prcp` AS FLOAT64) * 25.4 AS precip_mm
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- restrict shards externally when querying the view; keep all shards by default
  TRUE
  -- Exclude NULLs and documented sentinel/missing values (99.99 per schema) and any negative/implausible values
  AND `prcp` IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(`prcp` AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(`prcp` AS FLOAT64) <> 99.99
  -- keep non-negative precipitation measurements (0.00 is valid: no precipitation)
  AND SAFE_CAST(`prcp` AS FLOAT64) >= 0
daily_precip_records.description: All daily precipitation measurement records with their station identifier and date, filtered to records that have valid precipitation values (exclude NULL/invalid codes such as 99.99 or other schema-specific missing-value codes). Do not aggregate; keep one row per station-date.

daily_observations_sel.name: daily_observations_sel
daily_observations_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  'Rochester' AS location,
  NULLIF(temp, 9999.9) AS temperature,
  NULLIF(prcp, 99.99) AS precipitation,
  -- wdsp stored as string in some shards; try safe_cast else NULL; also 999.9 indicates missing in docs
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL THEN NULLIF(SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64), 999.9)
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS STRING) IS NOT NULL THEN NULLIF(SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64), 999.9)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS wind_speed
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2019' AND '2019'
  -- restrict to Rochester by station name via join to stations table: match stations with name containing 'Rochester'
  -- but BigQuery view must be a single SELECT body; use EXISTS with stations table
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` s
    WHERE s.usaf = stn
      AND (LOWER(s.name) LIKE '%rochester%' OR LOWER(s.name) LIKE '%rochester, ny%' OR LOWER(s.name) LIKE '%rochester ny%')
  )
  AND PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) BETWEEN DATE('2019-01-01') AND DATE('2019-03-31')

semantic_filters.location: equals Rochester (logical match; actual schema alignment will bind the column/value)

This relation restricts rows to the specified location (Rochester) and dates from 2019-01-01 through 2019-03-31 inclusive and yields one row per date with the raw observed numeric values (unrounded).

daily_observations_norm.name: daily_observations_norm
daily_observations_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical date (YYYY-MM-DD) built from GSOD year/mo/da fields
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d',
    CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo, 2, '0'), '-', LPAD(da, 2, '0'))
  ) AS date,

  -- canonical temperature in degrees Celsius
  -- gsod temp is in Fahrenheit with 9999.9 = missing; convert to C and return NULL when missing
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(temp AS FLOAT64) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN temp >= 9999 THEN NULL
    ELSE (temp - 32) * 5.0/9.0
  END AS temperature_c,

  -- canonical precipitation in centimeters
  -- gsod prcp is in inches with 99.99 = missing; treat .00 as 0.00; convert inches -> cm (1 in = 2.54 cm)
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(prcp AS FLOAT64) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN prcp >= 99 THEN NULL
    ELSE prcp * 2.54
  END AS precipitation_cm,

  -- canonical wind speed in meters/second
  -- gsod wdsp (mean wind) is in knots to tenths (string sometimes); missing = 999.9
  -- convert knots -> m/s: 1 knot = 0.514444 m/s
  CASE
    WHEN wdsp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '') AS FLOAT64) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN CAST(SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '') AS FLOAT64) AS FLOAT64) >= 999 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '') AS FLOAT64) * 0.514444
  END AS wind_speed_ms

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- lift suffix range out of the view (user should supply in queries against the view);
  -- keep all shards by default — but do not select literal single-day shards here.
  TRUE
daily_observations_norm.description: Normalize and canonicalize daily observation fields: cast/convert units if needed, handle NULLs, and produce canonical numeric values for temperature (°C), precipitation (cm), and wind_speed (m/s). Keep one row per date (location stays Rochester).

normalized_valid_temperature_observation.name: normalized_valid_temperature_observations
normalized_valid_temperature_observation.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- observation_id: compose from station identifiers + date to ensure row-level uniqueness across shards
  CONCAT(stn, '-', COALESCE(wban, ''), '-', year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0')) AS observation_id,
  -- station_id: keep station identifiers joinable (use stn and wban concatenated)
  CONCAT(stn, '-', COALESCE(wban, '')) AS station_id,
  -- observation_date: normalized DATE from year, month, day
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS observation_date,
  -- temperature_celsius: convert from Fahrenheit to Celsius when temp is a valid reading
  ROUND((temp - 32.0) * 5.0/9.0, 2) AS temperature_celsius,
  -- original_temperature_unit: source unit in the dataset (Fahrenheit)
  'F' AS original_temperature_unit
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- filter shards by year range lifted out of the view (keep generic; caller should add _TABLE_SUFFIX filter)
  TRUE
  -- Exclude missing/invalid temp values per DDL: missing = 9999.9
  AND temp IS NOT NULL
  AND temp != 9999.9
  -- Exclude rows where count_temp indicates no observations (if provided and zero)
  AND (count_temp IS NULL OR count_temp > 0)
  -- Ensure date parseable
  AND SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) IS NOT NULL
normalized_valid_temperature_observation.description: Normalize and filter observations: convert temperature values to a consistent unit if needed (or pass through if single unit), and exclude rows where temperature is NULL or marked invalid/missing by any validity indicator. nyc_zip_hours.name: nyc_zip_hours
nyc_zip_hours.body_sql:
SELECT
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(hour_ts, HOUR) AS hour_ts
FROM (
  -- distinct NYC zip codes from the public geo table
  SELECT DISTINCT zip_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes`
  WHERE state_code = 'NY'
    -- heuristic to restrict to NYC counties; lift any county list out of view in calling queries.
    AND county IN ('Kings', 'Queens', 'New York', 'Bronx', 'Richmond')
    AND zip_code IS NOT NULL
) AS z
CROSS JOIN (
  -- generate continuous sequence of hourly timestamps covering:
  -- at least 2015-01-01 00:00:00 through 2015-01-01 23:00:00, plus N_PRE hours prior.
  -- N_PRE should be provided by downstream queries; here we put a generous default span using parameters in calling queries.
  SELECT GENERATE_TIMESTAMP_ARRAY(
    -- start and end are to be replaced / bounded by downstream queries; defaults chosen to cover common needs
    TIMESTAMP('2014-07-16 00:00:00 UTC'),  -- 504 hours before 2015-01-01 00:00:00
    TIMESTAMP('2015-01-01 23:00:00 UTC'),
    INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  ) AS hours
) AS hrs,
UNNEST(hrs.hours) AS hour_ts
nyc_zip_hours.description: Generate all combinations of distinct NYC zip codes (from the geo zip code polygon set) and every hourly timestamp for the target date range needed by downstream windows. This produces one row per (zip_code, hour_ts) covering at least the 24 hours of 2015-01-01 and additionally any earlier hours required to compute lagged and moving-window metrics (e.g., up to 504 hours before the earliest target hour).

cleaned_trips.name: cleaned_trips
cleaned_trips.body_sql:
-- cleaned_trips: one row per trip with valid pickup datetime and coordinates

  -- Construct a stable trip_id from available fields: vendor + pickup timestamp + coords
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(vendor_id, 'NULL'), '--',
    CAST(pickup_datetime AS STRING), '--',
    CAST(pickup_longitude AS STRING), '--',
    CAST(pickup_latitude AS STRING)

  pickup_longitude,
  pickup_latitude
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2009' AND '2016'
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  -- reasonable NYC bounding box for longitude/latitude
  AND pickup_longitude BETWEEN -80 AND -70
  AND pickup_latitude BETWEEN  38 AND 45

UNION ALL

SELECT
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(vendor_id, 'NULL'), '--',
    CAST(pickup_datetime AS STRING), '--',
    CAST(pickup_longitude AS STRING), '--',
    CAST(pickup_latitude AS STRING)
  ) AS trip_id,
  pickup_datetime,

WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2013' AND '2016'
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_longitude BETWEEN -80 AND -70
  AND pickup_latitude BETWEEN  38 AND 45

UNION ALL

SELECT
  -- fhv trips use location_id instead of coords; exclude rows without coords
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(CAST(location_id AS STRING), 'NULL'), '--',
    CAST(pickup_datetime AS STRING)
  , '--NULL--NULL') AS trip_id,

  AND location_id IS NOT NULL

SELECT

  AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1763' AND '2024'

ghcn_stations_within_radius.name: ghcn_stations_within_radius
ghcn_stations_within_radius.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS station_id,
  s.latitude AS station_lat,
  s.longitude AS station_lon,
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_*` AS d
    WHERE d.id = s.id
      AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1763' AND '2024'
      AND d.element = 'PRCP'
    LIMIT 1

FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_stations` AS s
WHERE ST_DISTANCE(
        ST_GEOGPOINT(s.longitude, s.latitude),
        ST_GEOGPOINT(-74.0060, 40.7128)

This selects candidate stations by geographic distance and existence of precipitation data, but does not pick the nearest yet.

round_trips_normalized_times.name: round_trips_normalized_times
round_trips_normalized_times.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(r.trip_id AS STRING) AS trip_id,
  CAST(r.start_station_id AS INT64) AS start_station_id,
  CAST(r.end_station_id AS INT64) AS end_station_id,
  -- Normalize input start_time/end_time to TIMESTAMP type (supports string or TIMESTAMP inputs)
  CASE
    WHEN r.start_time IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(r.start_time AS TIMESTAMP) IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(r.start_time AS TIMESTAMP)
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(r.start_time AS STRING) IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(r.start_time AS TIMESTAMP)
    ELSE TIMESTAMP(r.start_time)
  END AS start_time_ts,
  CASE
    WHEN r.end_time IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(r.end_time AS TIMESTAMP) IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(r.end_time AS TIMESTAMP)
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(r.end_time AS STRING) IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(r.end_time AS TIMESTAMP)
    ELSE TIMESTAMP(r.end_time)
  END AS end_time_ts,
  -- numeric epoch seconds for convenient time-difference calculations
  CASE
    WHEN r.start_time IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE UNIX_SECONDS(
      CASE
        WHEN SAFE_CAST(r.start_time AS TIMESTAMP) IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(r.start_time AS TIMESTAMP)
        ELSE TIMESTAMP(r.start_time)
      END
    )
  END AS start_time_epoch,
  CASE
    WHEN r.end_time IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE UNIX_SECONDS(
      CASE
        WHEN SAFE_CAST(r.end_time AS TIMESTAMP) IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(r.end_time AS TIMESTAMP)
        ELSE TIMESTAMP(r.end_time)
      END
    )
  END AS end_time_epoch
FROM
  `round_trips_raw` AS r
round_trips_normalized_times.description: Normalize/cast the start_time and end_time to a consistent timestamp type and canonicalize station ids; produce any derived numeric epoch seconds if useful for time-difference calculations.

pairwise_time_neighbors.name: pairwise_time_neighbors
pairwise_time_neighbors.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.trip_id AS trip_id,
  r.start_station_id AS start_station_id,
  r.end_station_id AS end_station_id,
  -- determine if there exists at least one other distinct trip at same start/end within +/-120s of both start and end
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `round_trips_normalized_times` AS other
    WHERE other.start_station_id = r.start_station_id
      AND other.end_station_id = r.end_station_id
      AND other.trip_id != r.trip_id
      AND ABS(other.start_time_epoch - r.start_time_epoch) <= 120
      AND ABS(other.end_time_epoch - r.end_time_epoch) <= 120
  ) AS is_in_group,
  -- count of distinct other trips (including the trip itself if you consider group size >=1). We count all trips that satisfy the pairwise time proximity, including the base trip, so group_member_count >=1 for any trip (will be 1 if no neighbors)
  (
    SELECT COUNT(1)
    FROM `round_trips_normalized_times` AS other
    WHERE other.start_station_id = r.start_station_id
      AND other.end_station_id = r.end_station_id
      AND ABS(other.start_time_epoch - r.start_time_epoch) <= 120
      AND ABS(other.end_time_epoch - r.end_time_epoch) <= 120
  ) AS group_member_count
FROM `round_trips_normalized_times` AS r
pairwise_time_neighbors.description: For each trip, find whether there exists at least one other distinct trip (same start_station and end_station because these are round trips) whose start_time is within 120 seconds AND whose end_time is within 120 seconds. Produce a boolean flag indicating membership in a group (group_size>=2) and also the group membership count if desired.

trees_nyc_year_filtered.name: trees_nyc_year_filtered
trees_nyc_year_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key/id columns
  recordid AS tree_id,

  -- observation year derived from table suffix to allow querying across shards
  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS obs_year,

  -- alive flag: interpret 'status' where common values include 'Alive'/'Dead' (case-insensitive)
  -- keep as BOOLEAN-like INT (1 = alive, 0 = not alive/unknown) — user asked for is_alive_flag (no type specified)
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(status) = 'alive' THEN TRUE
    WHEN LOWER(status) = 'dead' THEN FALSE
    ELSE NULL
  END AS is_alive_flag,

  -- raw species string from the source
  spc_common AS species_name_raw,

  -- possible species key if available in the source (carry through cb_new as an example of a key-like field)
  cb_new AS species_key_if_any,

  -- restrict to New York City by borough presence and return a normalized city name
  -- include only records from the 2 requested years via _TABLE_SUFFIX filter
  CASE
    WHEN borough IS NOT NULL AND borough != '' THEN 'New York City'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS location_city

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('1995', '2015')
  AND borough IS NOT NULL
  AND borough != ''
trees_nyc_year_filtered.description: Subset of tree observation records restricted to New York City and to the years 1995 or 2015, keeping alive/dead status, species name, and any key linking to tree_species. One row per original tree observation.

trees_ny_years_sel.name: trees_ny_years_sel

  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS STRING) AS year,
  spc_latin AS latin_name,
  spc_common AS common_name,
  -- status_alive_flag: true if status indicates alive (case-insensitive contains 'alive' or 'living' or 'dead' -> false)
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(status) IN ('alive','living','alive ') THEN TRUE
    WHEN LOWER(status) IN ('dead','dead ') THEN FALSE
    -- common encodings: use spc_common/status heuristics: if status contains 'dead' mark false, otherwise treat non-empty as true
    WHEN LOWER(status) LIKE '%dead%' THEN FALSE
    WHEN LOWER(status) LIKE '%alive%' THEN TRUE
    WHEN status IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE TRUE
  END AS status_alive_flag
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('1995','2015')
  -- restrict to records that are in New York by borough field presence (borough not null)
  AND (borough IS NOT NULL OR location IS NOT NULL OR longitude IS NOT NULL OR latitude IS NOT NULL)
