species_name_norm.description: Normalize species name fields: exclude records with empty or null latin name and produce an uppercase latin name field; keep common name as-is (may be null).

species_year_counts_agg.name: species_year_counts_agg
species_year_counts_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  UPPER(COALESCE(t.spc_latin, t.species, NULL)) AS latin_name_upper,
  COALESCE(t.spc_common, t.species, NULL) AS common_name,
  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS year,
  COUNT(1) AS total_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(COALESCE(t.status, '')) IN ('alive','l','live') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS alive_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(COALESCE(t.status, '')) IN ('dead','d') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dead_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*` AS t
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1995' AND '2015'
GROUP BY latin_name_upper, common_name, year
species_year_counts_agg.description: For each species (by latin_name_upper and common_name) and year, compute counts: total records, alive count, and dead count.

bike_trips_2016.name: bike_trips_2016
bike_trips_2016.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(CONCAT(CAST(starttime AS STRING), '|', CAST(bikeid AS STRING), '|', CAST(start_station_id AS STRING), '|', CAST(end_station_id AS STRING)) AS STRING) AS trip_id,
  start_station_id AS start_station_id,
  start_station_name AS start_station_name,
  start_station_latitude AS start_lat,
  start_station_longitude AS start_lon,
  end_station_id AS end_station_id,
  tripduration AS trip_duration_seconds,
  DATE(starttime) AS trip_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2016
bike_trips_2016.description: All Citi Bike trip records from calendar year 2016 with needed fields (start station id, start station name, start station latitude/longitude, trip duration, route identifiers like start->end). This is a filtered cohort limited to trips in 2016 and normalized times/durations as stored.

taxi_trips_2016.name: taxi_trips_2016
taxi_trips_2016.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- construct a taxi_trip_id from pickup_datetime + dropoff_datetime + pickup coords to be stable per trip
  CONCAT(CAST(pickup_datetime AS STRING), '|', CAST(dropoff_datetime AS STRING), '|',
         CAST(IFNULL(pickup_latitude, -9999) AS STRING), ',', CAST(IFNULL(pickup_longitude, -9999) AS STRING),
         '|', CAST(IFNULL(dropoff_latitude, -9999) AS STRING), ',', CAST(IFNULL(dropoff_longitude, -9999) AS STRING)
  ) AS taxi_trip_id,

  -- prefer location id fields if they exist; otherwise use coords as "lat,lon"
  -- lift any literal defaults out of the view (no literals specific to filtering year here)
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(NULL AS INT64) IS NOT NULL THEN NULL  -- placeholder to keep view reusable; real location IDs are not present in this schema
    ELSE CONCAT(CAST(pickup_latitude AS STRING), ',', CAST(pickup_longitude AS STRING))
  END AS pickup_location_id_or_coords,

  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(NULL AS INT64) IS NOT NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CONCAT(CAST(dropoff_latitude AS STRING), ',', CAST(dropoff_longitude AS STRING))
  END AS dropoff_location_id_or_coords,

  -- trip duration in seconds: difference between dropoff and pickup timestamps
  CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS INT64) AS taxi_duration_seconds,

  -- trip_date as the calendar date of pickup
  DATE(pickup_datetime) AS trip_date

FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160101' AND '20161231'
  -- ensure we have timestamps and at least one of the coordinate pairs to be useful for routing comparisons
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND ((pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL)
       OR (dropoff_latitude IS NOT NULL AND dropoff_longitude IS NOT NULL))
  -- only keep positive, nonzero durations
  AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) > 0
taxi_trips_2016.description: All yellow taxi trip records from calendar year 2016 with origin/destination identifiers or coordinates and trip duration (or travel time) needed to compute comparable route average times.

station_start_counts.name: station_start_counts
station_start_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  start_station_id,
  start_station_name,
  COUNT(1) AS trip_start_count_2018
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2018
GROUP BY
  start_station_id,
  start_station_name
station_start_counts.description: Count of trips starting at each station during 2018 (one row per start station), using the filtered 2018 trips.

top_station_trips_by_dow_hour.name: top_station_trips_by_dow_hour
top_station_trips_by_dow_hour.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.start_station_id AS start_station_id,
  CAST(EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM TIMESTAMP(starttime)) AS INT64) AS day_of_week,
  CAST(EXTRACT(HOUR FROM TIMESTAMP(starttime)) AS INT64) AS hour_of_day,
  COUNT(1) AS trip_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips` t
JOIN
  `station_start_counts` s
ON
  t.start_station_id = s.start_station_id
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TIMESTAMP(starttime)) = 2018
GROUP BY
  s.start_station_id,
  day_of_week,
  hour_of_day
top_station_trips_by_dow_hour.description: For trips in 2018 that started at the chosen top station, compute counts grouped by numeric day-of-week and by hour-of-day (derived from the trip start timestamp). This produces per-(day_of_week) and per-(hour_of_day) counts (one row per grouping key). The final answer will pick the day_of_week and hour_of_day with the highest counts from these groups.

yellow_trips_raw_selection.name: yellow_trips_raw_selection
yellow_trips_raw_selection.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- unique id for the trip: compose from table suffix + pickup timestamp + vendor if no explicit id exists
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, "-", CAST(UNIX_MICROS(pickup_datetime) AS STRING), "-", IFNULL(vendor_id, "0")) AS trip_id,
  -- vendor flag carried through
  vendor_id AS vendor_flag,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  -- duration in seconds (allow fractional seconds -> integer)
  CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS INT64) AS trip_duration_seconds,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id,
  -- preserve other monetary/flag fields useful for later validity checks
  TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(rate_code, store_and_fwd_flag, payment_type, fare_amount, extra, mta_tax, tip_amount, tolls_amount, imp_surcharge, total_amount, data_file_year, data_file_month)) AS other_relevant_fields_for_validity
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- date range filter: lift literal out of view (user should supply bounds when querying view)
  -- here we keep the predicate placeholders as generic comparisons; users should replace 'YYYY' with actual values.
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023'
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  -- cohort filters:
  AND passenger_count > 3
  AND trip_distance >= 10
  AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) > 0
yellow_trips_raw_selection.description: Select raw Yellow taxi trip records and apply base cohort filters: pickup datetime within the date range (inclusive), passenger count > 3, trip distance >= 10, and trip duration > 0. Do not apply dataset-specific validity flags here (those are handled in a later step).

normalized_trips.name: normalized_trips
normalized_trips.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- trip identifier: construct from available fields to ensure uniqueness across shards
  COALESCE(
    CAST(CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, "-", SAFE_CAST(FLOOR(UNIX_MICROS(pickup_datetime) / 1000) AS STRING), "-", SAFE_CAST(CAST(pickup_datetime AS TIMESTAMP) AS STRING)) AS STRING),
    CONCAT(CAST(data_file_year AS STRING), "-", CAST(data_file_month AS STRING), "-", SAFE_CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER() AS STRING))
  ) AS trip_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  -- borough: coerce pickup_location_id to a borough-like value. Keep NULLs as NULL.
  -- preserve original string id so view stays joinable; alias as pickup_borough per spec.
  SAFE_CAST(pickup_location_id AS STRING) AS pickup_borough,
  -- monetary fields: coerce NULLs to 0 for amounts where appropriate, but leave tip_amount NULL if explicitly NULL
  IFNULL(tip_amount, 0) AS tip_amount,
  IFNULL(fare_amount, 0) AS fare_amount,
  -- tip_rate: tip_amount / fare_amount when fare_amount > 0, else NULL
  CASE
    WHEN fare_amount IS NOT NULL AND fare_amount > 0 THEN IFNULL(tip_amount, 0) / fare_amount
    ELSE NULL
  END AS tip_rate,
  -- is_no_tip: TRUE when tip_amount is 0 or NULL/zero-equivalent? Define as TRUE when tip_amount = 0
  SAFE_CAST(CASE WHEN IFNULL(tip_amount, 0) = 0 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS BOOL) AS is_no_tip
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023'
normalized_trips.description: Normalize and canonicalize each trip row: compute tip_rate (defined as tip_amount / fare_amount where fare_amount > 0, or NULL if fare_amount <= 0), coerce types and handle NULLs for borough identifiers and monetary fields as needed. Keep one row per trip.

raw_trips_cohort.name: raw_trips_cohort
raw_trips_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- unique id per trip: compose from available fields to ensure joinability
  CONCAT(COALESCE(CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS STRING), ''), '_',
         COALESCE(CAST(data_file_year AS STRING), ''), '_',
         COALESCE(CAST(data_file_month AS STRING), ''), '_',
         COALESCE(CAST(FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m%d%H%M%S', pickup_datetime) AS STRING), ''),
         '_', COALESCE(CAST(FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m%d%H%M%S', dropoff_datetime) AS STRING), ''),
         '_', COALESCE(CAST(fare_amount AS STRING), ''),
         '_', COALESCE(CAST(passenger_count AS STRING), '')
        ) AS trip_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  COALESCE(tip_amount, 0) AS tip_amount,
  COALESCE(tolls_amount, 0) AS tolls_amount,
  COALESCE(mta_tax, 0) AS mta_tax,
  COALESCE(fare_amount, 0) AS fare_amount,
  COALESCE(total_amount, 0) AS total_amount,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023'
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  -- both datetimes must fall within the queried shards' date range:
  -- lift specific date-range literals out of the view (use shard suffix filter above)
  -- basic validity and cohort filters:
  AND passenger_count > 5
  AND trip_distance >= 10.0
  AND tip_amount IS NOT NULL AND tip_amount >= 0
  AND tolls_amount IS NOT NULL AND tolls_amount >= 0
  AND mta_tax IS NOT NULL AND mta_tax >= 0
  AND fare_amount IS NOT NULL AND fare_amount >= 0
  AND total_amount IS NOT NULL AND total_amount >= 0
  AND dropoff_datetime > pickup_datetime
UNION ALL
SELECT
  CONCAT(COALESCE(CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS STRING), ''), '_',
         COALESCE(CAST(data_file_year AS STRING), ''), '_',
         COALESCE(CAST(data_file_month AS STRING), ''), '_',
         COALESCE(CAST(FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m%d%H%M%S', pickup_datetime) AS STRING), ''),
         '_', COALESCE(CAST(FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m%d%H%M%S', dropoff_datetime) AS STRING), ''),
         '_', COALESCE(CAST(fare_amount AS STRING), ''),
         '_', COALESCE(CAST(passenger_count AS STRING), '')
        ) AS trip_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  COALESCE(tip_amount, 0) AS tip_amount,
  COALESCE(tolls_amount, 0) AS tolls_amount,
  COALESCE(mta_tax, 0) AS mta_tax,
  COALESCE(fare_amount, 0) AS fare_amount,
  COALESCE(total_amount, 0) AS total_amount,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_green_trips_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2014' AND '2023'
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND passenger_count > 5
  AND trip_distance >= 10.0
  AND tip_amount IS NOT NULL AND tip_amount >= 0
  AND tolls_amount IS NOT NULL AND tolls_amount >= 0
  AND mta_tax IS NOT NULL AND mta_tax >= 0
  AND fare_amount IS NOT NULL AND fare_amount >= 0
  AND total_amount IS NOT NULL AND total_amount >= 0
  AND dropoff_datetime > pickup_datetime
raw_trips_cohort.description: Select raw taxi trip records restricted to trips whose pickup and dropoff datetimes fall within the queried date range, have passenger_count > 5, trip_distance >= 10.0, tip_amount >= 0, tolls_amount >= 0, mta_tax >= 0, fare_amount >= 0, total_amount >= 0, and where dropoff datetime is strictly after pickup datetime. Do not compute derived fields here — just filter rows.

trip_time_and_speed.name: trip_time_and_speed
trip_time_and_speed.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Construct a unique trip_id from available fields: vendor + pickup timestamp + dropoff timestamp + pickup_location (keeps joinability)
  CONCAT(vendor_id, "-", CAST(pickup_datetime AS STRING), "-", CAST(dropoff_datetime AS STRING), "-", COALESCE(pickup_location_id, "null")) AS trip_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  -- duration in seconds (dropoff - pickup)
  CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS INT64) AS trip_duration_seconds,
  -- duration in hours as a floating value (seconds / 3600). Protect against zero/negative durations by allowing non-positive to remain (caller can filter).
  SAFE_DIVIDE(CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS FLOAT64), 3600.0) AS trip_duration_hours,
  -- preserve trip distance as provided
  trip_distance,
  -- speed in miles per hour: distance divided by duration in hours. Use SAFE_DIVIDE to avoid div-by-zero.
  SAFE_DIVIDE(trip_distance, SAFE_DIVIDE(CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS FLOAT64), 3600.0)) AS speed_mph,
  tip_amount,
  fare_amount,
  total_amount,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- leave year/month range literal OUT of the view per instructions; consumer must filter _TABLE_SUFFIX.
  -- Basic validity filters kept generic: timestamps present and pickup <= dropoff
  pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) IS NOT NULL
trip_time_and_speed.description: Compute per-trip normalized temporal and speed measures: trip duration in seconds (dropoff - pickup) and trip duration in hours, and driving speed in miles per hour as trip_distance divided by duration in hours. Preserve original monetary and identifier fields for later joins/filters.

station_rows.name: station_rows
station_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  borough_name AS borough
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.stations`
WHERE
  station_id IS NOT NULL
  AND borough_name IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  station_id,
  borough_name
HAVING
  COUNT(DISTINCT borough_name) = 1
station_rows.description: All subway station records restricted to stations that have a single assigned borough (use the station's borough attribute as provided). Each row represents one station entity with its borough key.

entrance_rows.name: entrance_rows
entrance_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Use a synthetic entrance_id built from station_name + entrance coordinates + corner to ensure uniqueness per entrance.
  -- Carry station_name as station_id to keep joinability to station-level views.
  CONCAT(station_name, '||', CAST(entrance_lat AS STRING), '||', CAST(entrance_lon AS STRING), '||', IFNULL(corner, '')) AS entrance_id,
  station_name AS station_id,
  -- is_entry comes from the entry boolean column
  IF(entry IS NULL, FALSE, entry) AS is_entry,
  -- is_ada_compliant comes from ada_compliant boolean column
  IF(ada_compliant IS NULL, FALSE, ada_compliant) AS is_ada_compliant
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.station_entrances`
entrance_rows.description: All entrance/entry records for subway stations, each row indicating whether that entrance is marked as an actual entry and whether it is ADA-compliant (boolean flags).

station_ada_flag.name: station_ada_flag
station_ada_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.station_id AS station_id,
  -- True if any entrance for the station is both an actual entry and ADA-compliant
  EXISTS(
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.station_entrances` e
    WHERE e.station_name = s.station_name
      AND e.entry = TRUE
      AND e.ada_compliant = TRUE
  ) AS has_ada_entry
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.stations` s
station_ada_flag.description: For each station, determine whether the station has at least one entrance that is both an actual entry and ADA-compliant. Produces one row per station with a boolean flag indicating ADA-entry presence.

raw_trips_cohort.name: raw_trips_cohort
raw_trips_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  bike_number AS bike_id,
  start_station_id,
  end_station_id,
  NULL AS trip_distance_column_if_present,
  NULL AS start_lat,
  NULL AS start_lon,
  NULL AS end_lat,
  NULL AS end_lon
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
WHERE
  bike_number IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    -- keep rows that have at least some distance-relevant data:
    -- either an explicit trip distance column (not present in this table) OR origin/destination station ids
    start_station_id IS NOT NULL
    OR end_station_id IS NOT NULL
  )
raw_trips_cohort.description: All trip records from the bikeshare trips dataset restricted to rows with a non-null bike identifier and to trips that have at least some distance-relevant data (either an explicit trip distance value or origin/destination station identifiers). Do not compute distances here, just filter out clearly unusable rows.

station_locations.name: station_locations
station_locations.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  latitude AS station_lat,
  longitude AS station_lon
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations`
station_locations.description: One row per station from the stations dataset providing station identifier and its geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude). This relation supplies coordinates to compute distances for trips that reference stations.

trips_normalized.name: trips_normalized
trips_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(t.trip_id AS INT64) AS trip_id,
  -- ensure start_timestamp is a proper TIMESTAMP; use start_date column from source table
  TIMESTAMP(t.start_date) AS start_timestamp,
  -- year_month as YYYYMM string from start_timestamp
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m', TIMESTAMP(t.start_date)) AS year_month,
  -- duration in minutes as NUMERIC (preserve fractional minutes)
  SAFE_CAST(t.duration_sec AS NUMERIC) / 60.0 AS trip_duration_minutes
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips` AS t
trips_normalized.description: Normalize and project trip-level fields: cast/ensure start timestamp is a proper datetime, compute year_month as YYYYMM string from the start timestamp, and convert trip duration into minutes (numeric). Preserve original trip_id and start_timestamp.

first_last_trip_per_month.name: first_last_trip_per_month
first_last_trip_per_month.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id AS trip_id,
  t.year_month AS year_month,
  t.start_timestamp AS start_timestamp,
  t.trip_duration_minutes AS trip_duration_minutes,
  -- rank 1 = earliest in month
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.year_month ORDER BY t.start_timestamp ASC) AS rank_asc,
  -- rank 1 = latest in month
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.year_month ORDER BY t.start_timestamp DESC) AS rank_desc
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips` AS raw
JOIN
  -- prefer using existing normalized view if available; fallback to computed fields from raw table
  (
    SELECT
      trip_id,
      start_date AS start_timestamp,
      FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', start_date) AS year_month,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(duration_sec, 60) AS trip_duration_minutes
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
  ) AS t
ON raw.trip_id = t.trip_id
first_last_trip_per_month.description: Within each year_month, rank trips by start_timestamp to identify the earliest (first) and latest (last) trip rows so their trip_duration_minutes can be selected. Produce one row per trip with its rank positions so callers can pick first and last.

regions_master.name: regions_master
regions_master.body_sql:
SELECT
  region_id,
  name AS region_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_regions`
regions_master.description: All regions with their identifying key and region name; one row per region. (This provides region name to join to rides.)

rides_with_region.name: rides_with_region
rides_with_region.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id AS trip_id,
  t.start_date AS start_time,
  t.duration_sec AS duration,
  t.start_station_id AS start_station_id,
  t.member_gender AS gender,
  r.region_id AS region_id,
  r.name AS region_name
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` AS t
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info` AS s
  ON CAST(t.start_station_id AS STRING) = s.station_id
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_regions` AS r
  ON s.region_id = r.region_id
WHERE DATE(t.start_date) BETWEEN @start_date AND @end_date
rides_with_region.description: Join the date-filtered rides to their region rows to attach region identifiers/names to each ride row.

trips_2017_enddate_sel.name: trips_2017_enddate_sel
trips_2017_enddate_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  end_date,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM end_date) AS end_month,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(duration_sec, 60) AS duration_minutes,
  subscriber_type AS user_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM end_date) = 2017
trips_2017_enddate_sel.description: Select trips whose trip end date falls in the year 2017, keeping trip duration (in minutes) and user type and the month number of the end date.

monthly_user_minutes_agg.name: monthly_user_minutes_agg
monthly_user_minutes_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM end_date) AS end_month,
  subscriber_type AS user_type,
  SUM(duration_sec)/60.0 AS month_minutes
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
GROUP BY
  end_month,
  user_type
monthly_user_minutes_agg.description: For each month (1-12) and user type, sum trip durations (minutes). This produces one row per month and user_type with total minutes in that month.

monthly_user_minutes_pivot.name: monthly_user_minutes_pivot
monthly_user_minutes_pivot.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(end_month AS STRING) AS end_month,
  COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN user_type = 'Customer' THEN month_minutes END), 0) AS customer_month_minutes,
  COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN user_type = 'Subscriber' THEN month_minutes END), 0) AS subscriber_month_minutes
FROM
  `monthly_user_minutes_agg`
GROUP BY
  end_month
monthly_user_minutes_pivot.description: Pivot the per-month-per-user_type totals into one row per month with separate columns for Customer minutes and Subscriber minutes (missing values treated as zero or omitted if no trips).

trip_pairs_clay_sacramento.name: trip_pairs_clay_sacramento
trip_pairs_clay_sacramento.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(t.trip_id AS STRING) AS trip_id,
  t.trip_headsign AS trip_headsign,
  s.stop_name AS stop_name,
  st.stop_sequence AS stop_sequence,
  st.arrival_time AS arrival_time,
  st.departure_time AS departure_time
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_transit_muni.stop_times` AS st
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_transit_muni.stops` AS s
ON
  CAST(st.stop_id AS STRING) = s.stop_id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_transit_muni.trips` AS t
ON
  CAST(st.trip_id AS STRING) = t.trip_id
WHERE
  s.stop_name IN ('Clay St & Drumm St', 'Sacramento St & Davis St')
trip_pairs_clay_sacramento.description: Subset of stop-time rows that correspond to either of the two named stops ('Clay St & Drumm St' or 'Sacramento St & Davis St'), keeping their trip, stop identity, stop_sequence, arrival and departure times, and trip headsign (one row per matching stop occurrence).

population_records_2020_countries.name: population_records_2020_countries
population_records_2020_countries.body_sql:
SELECT
  mp5.country_code AS country_id,
  mp5.country_name AS country_name,
  mp5.year AS year,
  mp5.midyear_population AS population_total,
  -- sum under-20: include 5-year groups starting at 0,5,10,15 with age_group_indicator='-'
  (SELECT SUM(m2.midyear_population)
   FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_5yr_age_sex` m2
   WHERE m2.country_code = mp5.country_code
     AND m2.year = mp5.year
     AND m2.total_flag = 'A'
     AND m2.starting_age IN (0,5,10,15)
     AND m2.age_group_indicator = '-') AS population_under_20
FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_5yr_age_sex` mp5
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.country_names_area` cna
  ON cna.country_code = mp5.country_code
WHERE mp5.year = 2020
  AND mp5.total_flag = '*'
  -- restrict to entities that are individual countries by requiring a non-null, positive area
  AND cna.country_area IS NOT NULL
  AND cna.country_area > 0
  -- require total population present and non-zero
  AND mp5.midyear_population IS NOT NULL
  AND mp5.midyear_population <> 0
  -- require under-20 population present and non-zero (evaluate the same aggregation used above)
  AND (
    SELECT SUM(m3.midyear_population)
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_5yr_age_sex` m3
    WHERE m3.country_code = mp5.country_code
      AND m3.year = mp5.year
      AND m3.total_flag = 'A'
      AND m3.starting_age IN (0,5,10,15)
      AND m3.age_group_indicator = '-'
  ) IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    SELECT SUM(m4.midyear_population)
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_5yr_age_sex` m4
    WHERE m4.country_code = mp5.country_code
      AND m4.year = mp5.year
      AND m4.total_flag = 'A'
      AND m4.starting_age IN (0,5,10,15)
      AND m4.age_group_indicator = '-'
  ) <> 0
grain: one row per country_id (country_code) for year = 2020
population_records_2020_countries.description: Select population records for the year 2020 restricted to entities that are individual countries (exclude world/regions) and where midyear total population and under-20 population values are present and non-zero.

population_share_under_20.name: population_share_under_20
population_share_under_20.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.`country_code` AS country_id,
  m.`country_name` AS country_name,
  CAST(m.`midyear_population` AS NUMERIC) AS population_total,
  CAST(u.population_under_20 AS NUMERIC) AS population_under_20,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(CAST(u.population_under_20 AS NUMERIC), NULLIF(CAST(m.`midyear_population` AS NUMERIC), 0)) AS share_under_20
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population` AS m
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    `country_code`,
    `country_name`,
    `year`,
    SUM(CAST(`population` AS NUMERIC)) AS population_under_20
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific`
  WHERE
    `age` BETWEEN 0 AND 19
  GROUP BY
    `country_code`, `country_name`, `year`
) AS u
ON m.`country_code` = u.`country_code` AND m.`year` = u.`year`
grain: one row per country_id (per country-year from midyear_population)
population_share_under_20.description: Compute the share/percentage of the population that is under 20 for each country record, and normalize numeric types and handle division safely.

countries_ranked_by_share.name: countries_ranked_by_share
countries_ranked_by_share.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.country_code AS country_id,
  p.country_name AS country_name,
  p.midyear_population AS population_total,
  -- population_under_20 computed by summing ages 0-19 from the single-year ages table for the same country/year and both sexes
  (
    SELECT SUM(a.population)
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific` AS a
    WHERE a.country_code = p.country_code
      AND a.year = p.year
      AND a.age < 20
  ) AS population_under_20,
  -- share as a fraction (not percentage) to keep normalization flexible; lift any formatting out of the view
  SAFE_DIVIDE(
    (
      SELECT SUM(a.population)
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific` AS a
      WHERE a.country_code = p.country_code
        AND a.year = p.year
        AND a.age < 20
    ),
    p.midyear_population
  ) AS share_under_20,
  -- rank of the country by share_under_20 in descending order (ties get same rank)
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(
      (
        SELECT SUM(a.population)
        FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific` AS a
        WHERE a.country_code = p.country_code
          AND a.year = p.year
          AND a.age < 20
      ),
      p.midyear_population
    ) DESC
  ) AS rank_by_share
FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population` AS p
-- restrict to a single year if desired by the query that selects from this view; leave year selection outside the view
grain: one row per country_id per year (country_id carried; year available in source if needed)
countries_ranked_by_share.description: Rank countries by the share/percentage of population under 20 in descending order to enable selecting the top countries.

population_by_country_year_age_group.name: population_by_country_year_age_group
population_by_country_year_age_group.body_sql:
SELECT

  a.year,
  a.age,
  CASE WHEN a.age < @under_age_threshold THEN 'under_25' ELSE '25_plus' END AS age_group,
  a.population
FROM (
  -- aggregate sexes if present to get total population by country, year, age
  SELECT
    `country_code`,
    `country_name`,
    `year`,
    `age`,
    SUM(`population`) AS population
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific`
  GROUP BY `country_code`, `country_name`, `year`, `age`
) AS a
population_by_country_year_age_group.description: Select population counts (or shares if available) broken down by country, year, and age group (with an age or age_group indicator that allows identifying ages under 25 versus total). This is a filtered/cohort relation but does not apply the 2017 filter yet (keep all years to allow reuse).

population_under25_and_total_by_country_.name: population_under25_and_total_by_country_year

population_under25_and_total_by_country_.description: Aggregate the selected population rows to produce, for each country and year, the total population and the population aged under 25 (sum over ages < 25 or age_groups representing <25).

country_daily_counts.name: country_daily_counts
country_daily_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  IFNULL(`country_name`, `iso_3166_1_alpha_3`) AS country,
  `date` AS date,
  MAX(IFNULL(`cumulative_confirmed`, 0)) AS confirmed,
  MAX(IFNULL(`cumulative_recovered`, 0)) AS recovered
FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE (aggregation_level = 0 OR aggregation_level IS NULL)
  AND (country_name IS NOT NULL OR iso_3166_1_alpha_3 IS NOT NULL)
GROUP BY country, date
country_daily_counts.description: Select the per-country daily cumulative COVID-19 totals (confirmed, recovered) for all dates available; one row per country-date. This filters rows to the date of interest in a later step (do not apply date literal here).

recovery_rate_per_country_date.name: recovery_rate_per_country_date
recovery_rate_per_country_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  country AS country,
  date AS date,
  confirmed AS confirmed,
  recovered AS recovered,
  CASE
    WHEN confirmed IS NULL AND recovered IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN confirmed IS NULL AND recovered IS NOT NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN confirmed = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_DIVIDE(recovered, confirmed)
  END AS recovery_rate
FROM `country_daily_counts`
recovery_rate_per_country_date.description: Compute a normalized recovery rate measure for each country-date as recovered/confirmed, handling division-by-zero and nulls; keep country and date keys.

anosmia_weekly_county_values.name: anosmia_weekly_county_values
anosmia_weekly_county_values.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key columns / requested output
  sub_region_2 AS county_name,
  date,
  -- compute ISO week-year and ISO week start date so weeks can be attributed to 2019/2020 consistently
  CAST(FORMAT_DATE('%G', PARSE_DATE('%F', date)) AS INT64) AS iso_week_year,
  -- ISO week start (Monday) as DATE
  DATE_TRUNC(PARSE_DATE('%F', date), WEEK(MONDAY)) AS iso_week_start_date,
  -- anosmia search frequency (keep as-is; original column name is symptom_anosmia)
  CAST(NULLIF(symptom_anosmia, '') AS FLOAT64) AS search_frequency
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_2_weekly`
WHERE
  -- restrict to New York state sub_region_1 values that indicate New York (keep flexible)
  LOWER(COALESCE(sub_region_1, '')) LIKE '%new york%'
  -- restrict to the five NYC counties: Bronx, Kings County, New York (Manhattan), Queens, Richmond County
  AND LOWER(COALESCE(sub_region_2, '')) IN ('bronx', 'kings county', 'new york', 'queens', 'richmond county')
  -- restrict to iso_week_years 2019 or 2020 (compute from the date string)
  AND CAST(FORMAT_DATE('%G', PARSE_DATE('%F', date)) AS INT64) IN (2019, 2020)

semantic_filters.county_name: in ('Bronx County','Queens County','Kings County','New York County','Richmond County')

anosmia_weekly_county_values.description: Select weekly search-frequency records for the symptom 'Anosmia' limited to the five specified NYC counties and to dates falling in either 2019 or 2020. This relation returns one row per raw weekly record (before any per-week combining across counties). The selection will also include an ISO week-year and ISO week-start date (or equivalent calendar-week identifier) computed so weeks can be consistently attributed to 2019 or 2020 as specified upstream.

  AND symptom_depression IS NOT NULL

period_averages.description: For each period_label produce the average anxiety_symptom_level and average depression_symptom_level across the included weekly country rows. Exclude rows with NULL symptom values from the averages.

WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2010'

census2010_population_by_zip.description: Select 2010 census population counts for each ZIP area, including male and female population fields needed for summation; exclude rows with NULLs in those population fields here (leave summation to the next step).

scoring_plays_raw.name: scoring_plays_raw
scoring_plays_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key columns / grain
  game_id,
  period AS quarter,
  event_id AS play_id,

  -- raw play time
  game_clock,

  -- scoring team id: the team attributed for the event when points change
  team_id AS scoring_team_id,

  -- raw description text
  event_description AS description_raw,

  -- points scored from perspective of two specific teams: Wildcats and Fighting Irish.
  -- These are driven by team_alias matching literals lifted out of view (use placeholders via SELECT parameters in queries that use this view).
  -- Here we compute points credited to the scoring team and assign to the appropriate output columns.
  CASE
    WHEN team_alias = @WILDCATS_ALIAS THEN COALESCE(points_scored, 0.0)
    ELSE 0.0
  END AS points_scored_wildcats,
  CASE
    WHEN team_alias = @FIGHTING_IRISH_ALIAS THEN COALESCE(points_scored, 0.0)
    ELSE 0.0
  END AS points_scored_fighting_irish

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`

WHERE
  -- Select only plays that change the score:
  -- include any play with non-null and non-zero points_scored
  SAFE_CAST(points_scored AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(points_scored AS FLOAT64) != 0
scoring_plays_raw.description: Select all play-event rows that represent scoring events (any play that changes the score) for the games identified above. Include raw play time (quarter and game clock), scoring team identifier, play description text, points scored by the play for each team (points for offense and/or points against), and any player/drive identifiers needed to describe the play.

venues_list.name: venues_list

    `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_games_sr`
  WHERE

all_games_season_filtered.name: all_games_season_filtered

SELECT

  g.a_three_points_made AS away_threes

WHERE
  -- exclude tournament games by keeping rows where tournament IS NULL or empty
  (g.tournament IS NULL OR g.tournament = '')
  -- ensure this is a completed/recorded game (has points for both teams)
  AND g.h_points IS NOT NULL
  AND g.a_points IS NOT NULL
all_games_season_filtered.description: All game-level rows for regular/other games with their season, date, team identifiers, points, and three-pointers made by each team (kept at one row per game).

teams_lookup.name: teams_lookup
teams_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(t.team_id, h.team_id, a.team_id) AS team_id,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(t.market, '' ), NULLIF(t.name, ''), NULLIF(h.team_name, ''), NULLIF(a.team_name, ''), CONCAT(NULLIF(t.alias, ''), '')) AS team_display_name
FROM (
  -- canonical teams table (bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_teams)
  SELECT
    id AS team_id,
    market,
    name,
    alias
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_teams`
) t
FULL JOIN (
  -- historical teams seasons to pick a name when not present in canonical table
  SELECT
    team_id,
    market AS team_name
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_historical_teams_seasons`
) h
ON t.team_id = h.team_id
FULL JOIN (
  -- historical teams games (some team ids exist only here)

  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_historical_teams_games`

ON COALESCE(t.team_id, h.team_id) = a.team_id

teams_lookup.description: Mapping of team identifiers to canonical team display names used to build matchup strings.

side_consistent_shots.name: side_consistent_shots
side_consistent_shots.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_id,
  team_id,
  shot_type,
  event_coord_x,
  event_coord_y,
  -- normalize x to be distance from nearer baseline: if x < 564 keep x, else mirror across court width 1128
  CASE
    WHEN event_coord_x IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN event_coord_x
    ELSE 1128 - event_coord_x
  END AS adjusted_x,
  -- adjusted_y depends on which side the shot was from per spec:
  -- if event_coord_x < 564 then adjusted_y = 600 - event_coord_y else adjusted_y = event_coord_y
  CASE
    WHEN event_coord_x IS NULL OR event_coord_y IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN 600 - event_coord_y
    ELSE event_coord_y
  END AS adjusted_y,
  -- shot_attempt_flag: any shot event (shot_made TRUE/FALSE or three_point_shot TRUE) treated as attempt
  CASE
    WHEN shot_made IS NOT NULL OR three_point_shot IS NOT NULL THEN 1
    WHEN type IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(type) LIKE '%shot%' THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS shot_attempt_flag,
  -- shot_made_flag: 1 if shot_made is true, else 0
  CASE WHEN shot_made = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS shot_made_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
WHERE
  -- keep only play rows that are shot attempts (type or event_type indicating a shot, or shot_made flagged)
  (
    shot_made IS TRUE
    OR shot_made IS FALSE
    OR three_point_shot = TRUE
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(type, '')) LIKE '%shot%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(event_type, '')) LIKE '%shot%'
  )
  -- ensure coordinates present
  AND event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
  AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
  -- enforce "on correct side of the court" for the shooting team:
  -- We consider shots valid when event_coord_x indicates the team is attacking the nearer basket.
  -- That is, keep shots where event_coord_x < 1128 AND event_coord_x >= 0 (basic sanity) .
  AND event_coord_x BETWEEN 0 AND 1128
  AND event_coord_y BETWEEN 0 AND 600
side_consistent_shots.description: Normalize each shot's coordinates and filter to shots that are on the correct side of the court for the shooting team using the coordinate-side logic. Also compute adjusted_x and adjusted_y using the provided rules (adjusted_x = event_coord_x if event_coord_x < 564 else 1128 - event_coord_x; adjusted_y = 600 - event_coord_y if event_coord_x < 564 else event_coord_y).

shot_type_aggregates.name: shot_type_aggregates
shot_type_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.shot_type AS shot_type,
  AVG(s.adjusted_x) AS avg_x,
  AVG(s.adjusted_y) AS avg_y,
  AVG(s.shot_attempt_flag) AS avg_shot_attempts,
  AVG(s.shot_made_flag) AS avg_made_shots
FROM
  `side_consistent_shots` AS s
GROUP BY
  s.shot_type
shot_type_aggregates.description: Aggregate per shot_type: compute average adjusted_x, average adjusted_y, average shot attempts, and average made shots across events (one row per shot_type).

second_period_player_events.name: second_period_player_events
second_period_player_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  pbp.game_id AS game_id,
  pbp.season AS season,
  pbp.player_id AS player_id,
  pbp.team_id AS market_id,
  -- points: use points_scored when present; otherwise derive from shot_made + three_point_shot (1 or 2) or 0
  COALESCE(
    pbp.points_scored,
    CASE
      WHEN pbp.shot_made = TRUE AND pbp.three_point_shot = TRUE THEN 3
      WHEN pbp.shot_made = TRUE THEN 2
      WHEN pbp.event_type = 'free_throw' AND pbp.points_scored IS NULL THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS points,
  pbp.period AS period,
  pbp.event_id AS event_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr` AS pbp
WHERE
  pbp.period = 2
  AND pbp.season BETWEEN 2010 AND 2018
  -- restrict to scoring events or plays that produce points (keeps one row per scoring event/stat line)
  AND (
    pbp.points_scored IS NOT NULL
    OR pbp.shot_made = TRUE
    OR pbp.event_type = 'free_throw'
  )
second_period_player_events.description: All player scoring events restricted to the second period (period = 2) and to games whose season is between 2010 and 2018 inclusive. Keep one row per individual scoring event (or stat line row) so players can be counted distinctly later.

players_with_15plus_in_second_period.name: players_with_15plus_in_second_period
players_with_15plus_in_second_period.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_id AS player_id,
  p.team_id AS market_id,
  -- flag true if player scored >=15 points in the 2nd period in any game for this market
  MAX(CASE WHEN sp.quarter = 2 AND SAFE_CAST(sp.points_scored_wildcats AS NUMERIC) IS NOT NULL AND (
             -- points for player attributed in either points_scored_wildcats or points_scored_fighting_irish depending on team
             (p.team_id = sp.scoring_team_id AND COALESCE(sp.points_scored_wildcats, sp.points_scored_fighting_irish) >= 15)
             OR
             -- if scoring columns are per-team in scoring_plays_raw, fall back to points_scored_wildcats when team matches home/away mapping;
             -- keep logic simple: treat any scoring play in quarter 2 with points >=15 as meeting threshold for that scoring_team_id
             (sp.quarter = 2 AND COALESCE(sp.points_scored_wildcats, sp.points_scored_fighting_irish) >= 15 AND p.team_id = sp.scoring_team_id)
           ) THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END) AS met_15_points_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_players_games_sr` p
LEFT JOIN
  scoring_plays_raw sp
ON
  p.game_id = sp.game_id
  AND p.player_id = sp.play_id -- note: scoring_plays_raw.play_id represents the event/player identifier; join preserved to keep player-level linkage
GROUP BY
  p.player_id,
  p.team_id
players_with_15plus_in_second_period.description: For each player in each market, determine whether that player scored at least 15 points in the second period of any qualifying game — produce one row per player-market indicating a boolean/flag or indicator of meeting the >=15 threshold (distinct players are not collapsed across markets).

third_month_employment_observations.name: third_month_employment_observations
third_month_employment_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- county name: use geoid as county identifier if a separate name column isn't available in shards
  -- keep key/id columns so the view is joinable
  COALESCE(NULLIF(area_fips, ''), geoid) AS county,
  -- state: derive from the first two chars of geoid/area_fips when possible (FIPS state code)
  SUBSTR(COALESCE(area_fips, geoid), 1, 2) AS state,
  -- derive year and month from the shard suffix and the "third month" concept:
  -- _TABLE_SUFFIX values observed like '2000_q3' and '2018_q1' ; map quarter to month (q1->3, q2->6, q3->9, q4->12)
  CAST(SPLIT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '_')[OFFSET(0)] AS INT64) AS year,
  CASE SPLIT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '_')[OFFSET(1)]
    WHEN 'q1' THEN 3
    WHEN 'q2' THEN 6
    WHEN 'q3' THEN 9
    WHEN 'q4' THEN 12
    ELSE NULL
  END AS month,
  -- employment value: use the canonical month3_emplvl_* column pattern. Because concrete column names vary by industry,
  -- select the generic column named exactly 'month3_emplvl_11_agriculture_forestry_fishing_and_hunting' as an example employment measure.
  -- If different employment series are needed, lift literals out of the view and adjust calling query to choose the column.
  month3_emplvl_11_agriculture_forestry_fishing_and_hunting AS employment_value,
  -- preserve an observation identifier (grain) so each raw row is addressable/joinable
  -- Combine table suffix with geoid to form observation_id
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, ':', COALESCE(area_fips, geoid)) AS observation_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.*`
WHERE
  -- restrict to the years of interest (2000 and 2018) using _TABLE_SUFFIX (sharded tables)
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2000_q1' AND '2000_q4'
  OR _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2018_q1' AND '2018_q4'
  -- ensure we only keep rows that correspond to the third month of the quarter (q1..q4 mapping above)
  AND SPLIT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '_')[OFFSET(1)] IN ('q1','q2','q3','q4')
  -- require the employment value to be non-null to represent an observation
  AND month3_emplvl_11_agriculture_forestry_fishing_and_hunting IS NOT NULL
grain: observation_id (one row per raw observation per county per shard)
third_month_employment_observations.description: Select employment observations restricted to the state cohort and to the third month of each quarter (March, June, September, December) for the years of interest (2000 and 2018). Keep each raw observation row with its county, year, month, and employment value.

county_year_quarterly_avg.name: county_year_quarterly_avg
county_year_quarterly_avg.body_sql:
SELECT
  tmo.county AS county,
  tmo.year AS year,
  AVG(tmo.employment_value) AS avg_employment,
  COUNT(1) AS observations_count
FROM
  `third_month_employment_observations` AS tmo
GROUP BY
  tmo.county,
  tmo.year
HAVING
  COUNT(1) = 4
county_year_quarterly_avg.description: For each county and year, compute the average employment across the four third-month-of-quarter observations (one average per county-year). Exclude county-years that are missing any of the four required third-month observations.

wage_records_filtered.name: wage_records_filtered
wage_records_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(c.county_name, ', ', 'PA') AS geography,
  cbsa.name AS metropolitan_area,
  'ALL_INDUSTRIES' AS industry,
  'AVG_ANNUAL_WAGE' AS measure,
  CAST(SUBSTR(_TABLE_SUFFIX, 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year,
  -- pick a representative average annual wage column: avg_wkly_wage_11_... exists; annualize it by *52
  (avg_wkly_wage_11_agriculture_forestry_fishing_and_hunting * 52) AS value,
  -- row_id grain: combine table suffix + geoid + area_fips to form unique id per source row
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '_', geoid, '_', IFNULL(area_fips, '')) AS row_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2010_q*`
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.cbsa` AS cbsa
ON
  cbsa.cbsa_fips_code = SAFE_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(geoid, r'^(.{5})') AS STRING)
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.counties` AS c
ON
  c.county_fips_code = SUBSTR(geoid, 3, 3) AND c.state_fips_code = SUBSTR(geoid, 1, 2)
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2010_q1' AND '2010_q4'
  AND c.county_name = 'Allegheny'
  AND cbsa.name LIKE '%Pittsburgh%'
  AND avg_wkly_wage_11_agriculture_forestry_fishing_and_hunting IS NOT NULL
wage_records_filtered.description: Select wage data rows filtered to Allegheny County within the Pittsburgh metropolitan area, for the measure representing average annual wages, and for all industries. Keep rows for all years (we will pick specific years later).

filtered_trips.name: filtered_trips
filtered_trips.body_sql:

trips_in_2018_by_company_month.name: trips_in_2018_by_company_month

filtered_trips_2.name: filtered_trips_2

monthly_incident_counts.name: monthly_incident_counts

  incident_month

motor_theft_events_in_range.name: motor_theft_events_in_range

thefts_by_month.name: thefts_by_month
thefts_by_month.body_sql:
SELECT

FROM

yearly_max_monthly_thefts_candidate.name: yearly_max_monthly_thefts_candidate
yearly_max_monthly_thefts_candidate.body_sql:

years_2010_to_2016_max_monthly_thefts.name: years_2010_to_2016_max_monthly_thefts
years_2010_to_2016_max_monthly_thefts.body_sql:

  MAX(monthly_thefts) AS max_monthly_motor_thefts
FROM (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month,
    COUNTIF(primary_type = 'MOTOR VEHICLE THEFT') AS monthly_thefts
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) BETWEEN 2010 AND 2016
  GROUP BY year, month
)
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year ASC
years_2010_to_2016_max_monthly_thefts.description: Restrict the per-year maxima to the explicit years 2010 through 2016 and order results by year ascending. This final view applies the requested year filter and output ordering.

trades_long_side_filtered.name: trades_long_side_filtered
trades_long_side_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  TradeReportID AS trade_id,
  -- strategy is derived from TargetCompID; lift literals out of view (user should filter on these externally)
  -- For illustration we'll map known strings to strategies; keep NULL if not matched.
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%feeling-lucky%' THEN 'feeling-lucky'
    WHEN LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%momentum%' THEN 'momentum'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS strategy,
  -- side: take first element of Sides array if present; keep its Side value
  (SELECT s.Side FROM UNNEST(Sides) AS s LIMIT 1) AS side,
  -- intrinsic_value: compute as LastPx - StrikePrice (example intrinsic for option-like instruments)
  SAFE_SUBTRACT(LastPx, StrikePrice) AS intrinsic_value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report`
WHERE
  -- restrict to long side trades
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(Sides) AS s WHERE LOWER(s.Side) = 'long'
  )
  -- restrict to strategies of interest: feeling-lucky or momentum
  AND (
    LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%feeling-lucky%'
    OR LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%momentum%'
  )
trades_long_side_filtered.description: Select the subset of trade records restricted to long-side trades and to strategies of interest (feeling-lucky or momentum). Do not aggregate; keep one row per trade.

raw_trade_rows.name: raw_trade_rows

  LastPx AS openPrice,
  StrikePrice AS closePrice,
  Sides,
  -- Collect any remaining raw fields into a STRUCT for easy access downstream.
  STRUCT(
    SendingTime AS SendingTime,
    SenderCompID AS SenderCompID,
    Quantity AS Quantity,
    OrderID AS OrderID,
    TradeDate AS TradeDate,
    MaturityDate AS MaturityDate,
    CFICode AS CFICode
  ) AS other_raw_fields
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report`
raw_trade_rows.description: Select the raw trade rows from the provided dataset/document with all original fields extracted (including tradeID, tradeTimestamp, TargetCompID, symbol, openPrice, closePrice, Sides array and any other captured fields). This is a straight row-level subset (no aggregation or transformation).

exp_curr_rows_sel.name: exp_curr_rows_sel
exp_curr_rows_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(p.plot_state_code AS INT64) AS state_code,
  pe.evaluation_group_sequence_number AS eval_group,
  pet.evaluation_type AS eval_type,
  CASE
    WHEN pt.plot_inventory_year IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN pt.plot_phase_2_plot_number IS NULL THEN 0
    ELSE 1
  END AS is_macroplot_flag,
  -- lift literals out: base expansion factor source column from population (example: use 'area_used_to_calculate_all_expansion_factors')
  pn.area_used_to_calculate_all_expansion_factors AS base_expansion_factor,
  -- adjustment factor: use a generic population field if present; fall back to 1.0
  COALESCE(pn.phase_1_point_count_for_the_estimation_unit, 1.0) AS adjustment_factor,
  c.condition_status_code AS condition_status_code,
  c.reserved_status_code AS reserved_status_code,
  c.site_productivity_class_code AS site_productivity_class_code,
  p.plot_state_code_name AS state_name,
  -- row identifier (grain): compose from plot_sequence_number + condition_sequence if available
  CONCAT(CAST(p.plot_sequence_number AS STRING), "-", CAST(c.sequence_number AS STRING)) AS row_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.plot` p
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.condition` c
ON
  p.plot_sequence_number = c.plot_sequence_number
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.plot_tree` pt
ON
  p.plot_sequence_number = pt.plot_sequence_number
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population` pn
ON
  c.plot_sequence_number = pn.plot_sequence_number
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_type` pet
ON
  pn.evaluation_sequence_number = pet.evaluation_sequence_number
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_type` pe
ON
  pn.evaluation_sequence_number = pe.evaluation_sequence_number
WHERE
  pet.evaluation_type = 'EXPCURR'
exp_curr_rows_sel.description: Select only rows whose evaluation type equals the literal 'EXPCURR'. Keep all columns needed to determine plot type (macroplot vs subplot), expansion factor base, adjustment factor, state, evaluation group, condition/reserved/site codes, and state name.

conditions_2012_rows.name: conditions_2012_rows
conditions_2012_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  pe.evaluation_group_sequence_number AS eval_group_id,
  pe.evaluation_group AS evaluation_type,
  c.condition_status_code AS condition_status_code,
  pe.evaluation_group_description AS evaluation_description,
  c.state_code AS state_code,
  -- macroplot_acres and subplot_acres are not present explicitly in the provided DDL;
  -- use population_stratum.phase_1_point_count as a proxy for area-related measure if needed,
  -- but lift literals out of view: here we pass NULLs so downstream can set values.
  NULL AS macroplot_acres,
  NULL AS subplot_acres,
  -- carry a condition row identifier for grain (condition_row_id)
  c.sequence_number AS condition_row_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.condition` AS c
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_group` AS pe
ON
  c.state_code = pe.state_code
  -- no direct key provided between condition and evaluation_group in DDL;
  -- join on state_code to associate evaluation groups with conditions in the same state
WHERE
  c.inventory_year = 2012
  -- restrict to evaluation-group-level records: ensure evaluation_group_sequence_number exists
  AND pe.evaluation_group_sequence_number IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.row_kind: evaluation-group-condition (only rows that represent evaluation-group conditions)

conditions_2012_rows.description: Select all rows from the 2012 inventory that correspond to evaluation-group-level condition records (rows that link an evaluation group to a condition) and keep columns needed for later (evaluation group id/key, evaluation type, condition status code, evaluation description, state code, macroplot acres, subplot acres). Exclude any rows not from inventory year 2012.

sightings_filtered.name: sightings_filtered
sightings_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  gbifid AS sighting_id,
  eventdate AS date,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM eventdate) AS year,
  decimallatitude AS latitude,
  scientificname AS species
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
WHERE
  scientificname = @target_species
  AND decimallatitude > @lat_threshold
  AND eventdate IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.species: filter for species = 'Sterna paradisaea' (apply later during schema alignment)
semantic_filters.latitude: filter for latitude > 40 (apply later during schema alignment)

sightings_filtered.description: All sighting records restricted to the target species and to locations north of 40 degrees latitude, with the original date preserved and a derived calendar year. (No aggregation — one row per raw sighting event/record.)

ports_in_region_and_us_state.name: ports_in_region_and_us_state
ports_in_region_and_us_state.body_sql:
SELECT
  index_number AS port_id,
  region_number,
  port_geom AS port_geometry,
  s.geo_id AS us_state_id,
  s.state_name AS us_state_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_international_ports.world_port_index` p
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.states` s
ON
  ST_INTERSECTS(p.port_geom, s.state_geom)
WHERE
  region_number = '6585'
ports_in_region_and_us_state.description: Select ports that belong to the target region (region number = '6585') and that spatially lie within a U.S. state polygon (i.e., port geometry intersects a U.S. state geometry). Keep one row per port with its identifier, region number, port geometry, and the matched U.S. state identifier or name to indicate state membership.

building_aggregations_by_geo.name: building_aggregations_by_geo
building_aggregations_by_geo.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(state_name, "_", region_name) AS state_postal_code,
  region_name AS aggregation_key,
  'postal_code' AS aggregation_level_label,
  COUNT(1) AS total_buildings_available,
  AVG(percent_covered) AS avg_project_sunroof_coverage_pct,
  AVG(percent_qualified) AS avg_coverage_suitable_pct,
  SUM(IFNULL(number_of_panels_total, 0)) AS total_potential_panel_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(kw_total, 0)) AS total_potential_kw_capacity,
  SUM(IFNULL(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total, 0)) AS total_potential_generation_kwh,
  SUM(IFNULL(carbon_offset_metric_tons, 0) * 1000.0) AS total_co2_offset_kg,
  SUM(IFNULL(existing_installs_count, 0)) AS current_buildings_with_solar
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_postal_code`
GROUP BY
  state_name,
  region_name

UNION ALL

SELECT
  CONCAT(state_name, "_", region_name) AS state_postal_code,
  region_name AS aggregation_key,
  'census_tract' AS aggregation_level_label,
  COUNT(1) AS total_buildings_available,
  AVG(percent_covered) AS avg_project_sunroof_coverage_pct,
  AVG(percent_qualified) AS avg_coverage_suitable_pct,
  SUM(IFNULL(number_of_panels_total, 0)) AS total_potential_panel_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(kw_total, 0)) AS total_potential_kw_capacity,
  SUM(IFNULL(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total, 0)) AS total_potential_generation_kwh,
  SUM(IFNULL(carbon_offset_metric_tons, 0) * 1000.0) AS total_co2_offset_kg,
  SUM(IFNULL(existing_installs_count, 0)) AS current_buildings_with_solar
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_censustract`
GROUP BY
  state_name,
  region_name
building_aggregations_by_geo.description: Aggregate building-level metrics up to each geographic unit (one row per state + postal_code_block and one row per state + census_tract). For each aggregation unit compute total_buildings_available (count of buildings), avg_project_sunroof_coverage_pct (average of per-building project_sunroof_coverage_pct), avg_coverage_suitable_pct (average of per-building coverage_suitable_pct), totals of potential_panel_count, potential_kw_capacity, potential_generation_kwh, potential_co2_offset_kg, and current_buildings_with_solar (count of buildings with has_solar_flag true). Keep identifiers for state and the aggregation key and also include a column that labels the aggregation type (postal_code vs census_tract) to allow later unioning.
